entry.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network for Geodesic Computation and Visualization of Geodesic Spheres on Riemannian Manifolds
entry.summary: Visualizing geodesic structures associated with general Riemannian metrics is a challenging problem in computational differential geometry. In this work, we present a computational framework for visualizing geodesics and geodesic spheres on a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold equipped with the metric $g=\text{diag}(1,x^2,1), x>0$. The associated Christoffel symbols and curvature tensors are computed symbolically, and the resulting geodesic equations are solved using both \texttt{SciPy}'s numerical integration method and a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN). The two solutions are compared to assess the accuracy of the neural network approximation. We further develop geodesic spike diagrams and surface visualizations to illustrate the deformation of geodesic spheres relative to their Euclidean counterparts. Intrinsic Riemannian surface area and volume are estimated numerically using the induced metric and the Riemannian volume density, respectively. For the chosen metric and a geodesic ball of radius one, the computed area and volume are approximately $0.362\%$ and $0.364\%$ smaller than the corresponding Euclidean values at the base grid resolution. A grid-refinement study is also performed to examine the sensitivity of these estimates to numerical resolution. The proposed framework demonstrates how symbolic differential geometry, numerical integration, and PINNs can be combined to investigate and visualize geometric structures associated with Riemannian metrics.

entry.title: Spectra and strong decays of open charm-bottom $c\bar{b}q\bar{q}$ tetraquarks in an unequal-mass Born-Oppenheimer framework
entry.summary: We investigate the mass spectra and strong decay channels of $S$-wave open charm-bottom $c\bar{b}q\bar{q}$ ($q = u,d,s$) tetraquarks within the Born-Oppenheimer approximation. Extending our previous study of hidden heavy flavor tetraquarks, we account for the unequal-mass heavy quark sources and construct the effective potential based on independently optimized heavy-light orbitals. This makes the computational method more generally applicable. For the quantum numbers $J^P=0^+$, $1^+$, and $2^+$, we have obtained the spectra of the open charm-bottom $c\bar{b}q\bar{q}$ tetraquarks corresponding to color-singlet states constructed by coupling two color octets. The predicted masses exhibit systematic flavor-dependent shifts and characteristic hyperfine splittings. We also estimate partial widths for selected two-body open flavor decay channels using color-spin recoupling and a phenomenological decay prescription. The resulting channel-dependent decay modes, together with comparisons to other theoretical predictions, provide useful benchmarks for future theoretical investigations and experimental searches for open charm-bottom tetraquarks.

entry.title: Higher-order Approximate Symmetries
entry.summary: The Fushchych--Shtelen (FS) construction of approximate symmetries, based on a triangular system for the coefficients of a solution expansion, is extended to arbitrary order. A coefficient-map formulation establishes, under explicit hypotheses, a correspondence with the Baikov--Gazizov--Ibragimov (BGI) method. The two approaches are compared for a perturbed cubic wave equation. Nonlinearities admitting an FS point symmetry with prescribed projection onto the unperturbed dilation are classified through second order, up to equivalences. They comprise a power family and logarithmic families at exceptional exponents. Nonlinearities admitting second-order BGI point symmetries that continue this dilation are also classified. Among perturbations nontrivial at first order, these form a proper subfamily of one FS family; another family is admitted by both methods when the perturbation first enters at second order. Joint reduction by the Lorentz algebra and the inherited FS dilation yields explicit invariant solutions for all FS normal forms and recovers the first-order solutions of Fushchych and Shtelen. For the common family with a nontrivial first-order perturbation, the logarithmic corrections arise from expanding a power law with a perturbation-dependent exponent. Periodic traveling waves illustrate the long-scale validity of the FS expansion. The first correction is obtained by quadrature, second-order secular terms are identified, and phase renormalization yields bounded approximations. For integer-power members of the power family, the amplitude dependence of the corrected wavenumber agrees with the symmetry scaling weights.

entry.title: GRAVITY-RESOLVE: A comprehensive image reconstruction tool for Galactic Center observations with GRAVITY
entry.summary: We aim to improve and extend the imaging capabilities of the GRAVITY beam combiner instrument of ESOs VLTI with respect to reconstruction software in the Galactic Center. We revise and develop the image reconstruction code GRAVITY-RESOLVE $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$, which has been specifically developed to reconstruct stars in the Galactic Center with GRAVITY. The main objectives are to increase the limiting magnitude in GRAVITY images, reduce its computational runtime, and allow for a joint reconstruction of multiple, spatially separate datasets/pointings on sky. We apply $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ to recent GRAVITY data, featuring the implemented GRAVITY-faint mode as part of GRAVITY+, the upgrade of GRAVITY. We reconstruct visibility phases and amplitudes and present the first GRAVITY image reconstructed with $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ from these quantities. We demonstrate NIR mosaicking with $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ by jointly reconstructing nine separately acquired datasets of 2025 into a single image on a scale of $\simeq 3390\ \text{AU}\times 3390\ \text{AU}$, corresponding to $409.6\ \text{mas}\times 409.6\ \text{mas}$. With dedicated injection tests of point sources into GRAVITY data, we estimate the limiting magnitude to be $m_{\text{K}}\ \simeq\ 20.0$ within a radius of $25\ \text{mas}$ around the field center when reconstructing from closure phases and visibility amplitudes. We report on the discovery of two new faint stars in the Galactic Center: S303 and S304. Finally, we find a decrease in computational runtime by a factor of at least $\sim10$. With $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$, we demonstrate GRAVITYs capabilities for NIR imaging. We show that $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ is a fast, precise, and deep image reconstruction tool for Galactic Center observations, enabling the discovery of even more faint stars.

entry.title: Leaving the Cave by Breaking the Symmetry: Identifiable Structure Can Enable Cross-Lingual Generalization
entry.summary: Why do multilingual language models generalize across languages even without shared vocabulary? The Platonic Representation Hypothesis posits that models trained on different data, objectives, and modalities converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. Extending this intuition to representations inside a single multilingual model, we propose the Relational Identifiability Hypothesis: relations in a shared world can promote entity alignment by ruling out alternative cross-lingual correspondences, making corresponding entities more likely to become directly readable without an additional transformation. We test this hypothesis in a controlled bilingual Transformer whose two token-disjoint languages describe the same modular-arithmetic world. We find that the languages can develop a shared answer subspace without aligning corresponding numbers. Cross-lingual alignment emerges selectively when the available relations constrain number correspondences: subtraction makes zero task-level identifiable, inducing selective alignment, while an order-sensitive operation produces broad alignment across numbers. These patterns predict success in zero-shot cross-lingual transfer. Together, our results show that relational structure in a shared world can promote entity alignment and enable transfer.

entry.title: Beyond Reachability: When Edit Order Preserves Couplings in Graph Flow Matching
entry.summary: Shortest-path optimality does not guarantee that a memoryless graph generator preserves a prescribed source-target correspondence. We study whether reordering legal shortest edits can retain this correspondence without changing the pairing, mandatory edits, or sampling budget. Under a common Poisson clock, we establish an exact criterion for endpoint coupling recoverability: the source-blind Markov projection attains the unavoidable clock-error floor if and only if routes to distinct targets do not share graph states. Routes to the same target may merge without sacrificing endpoint fidelity. This characterization leads to an exact finite-state routing formulation and a legality-preserving scheduling procedure with recovery certificates. A marker-free construction demonstrates how shared edge structure can retain source distinctions, while a capacity-constrained family exhibits a sharp separation in paired error between edit orders with identical marginal error. Finally, a target-conditioned aliasing bound connects structural route design to the terminal fidelity of a learned graph-only generator. These results characterize when legal edit ordering can preserve a prescribed coupling under fixed operational costs.

entry.title: Using delays for prescribed-time static output feedback stabilization of LTI controllable and observable systems
entry.summary: This paper addresses a stabilization problem: can every controllable and observable LTI system be stabilized by static output feedback? To the best of our knowledge, we provide, for the first time, a solution to this problem. Furthermore, the proposed design achieves prescribed-time convergence to the origin, with the convergence time arbitrarily assigned a priori and independently of the initial condition. Two static output-feedback methods are developed. The first employs multiple artificial output delays with smooth time-varying gains and provides an explicit gain construction for every controllable and observable LTI system, based on a generalized controllability--observability Gramian introduced in this paper. The second combines constant-gain feedback of the current output with time-varying-gain feedback of a single artificially delayed output and also applies to every controllable and observable LTI system. Its simpler structure requires auxiliary parameters whose existence is guaranteed but whose explicit construction is not provided for general MIMO systems; for SISO systems, the constant current-output gain can be readily selected. The multiple-delay design is further extended to known bounded and fast-varying (without any constraints on the delay derivative) measurement delays, yielding fixed-time stabilization under a corresponding rank condition, with an assignable settling-time bound greater than three times the delay bound. For unknown constant measurement delays, fixed-time stabilization is established for systems with nilpotent state matrices. A numerical implementation is also presented. Numerical examples involving nonminimum-phase, flexible-structure, and cart--pole systems illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

entry.title: Genericity of singularities of solutions to quasilinear systems on compact sets
entry.summary: We study the genericity of singularities of types $A_2,A_3,D_4^\pm$ in solutions of the equations of gas dynamics and nonlinear geometrical optics. The sets of solutions satisfying the corresponding transversality conditions are proved to be open and dense in spaces of smooth and real-analytic solutions equipped with the Whitney topology on compact sets.

entry.title: Goldbach Representations in Quantum Optics and Metrology
entry.summary: We derive a relation between Goldbach representations and photon-number statistics in a quantum-optical setup. Considering an even-number Fock state injected into a stochastic beam splitter with uniformly distributed transmissivity and projections of the two output modes onto prime subspaces, we demonstrate that each successful outcome corresponds to an Goldbach representation and that the averaged detection probability is exactly proportional to the number of Goldbach representations. Then, employing the Hardy--Littlewood asymptotic formula, we demonstrate that the post-measurement state generated by a beam splitter with fixed transmissivity exhibits standard quantum limit scaling of the ultimate precision limit in terms of phase estimation, whereas an equally weighted superposition of Goldbach representations exhibits Heisenberg scaling. These results provide a quantum-optical realization of Goldbach representations and relate their statistics of with quantum metrology.

entry.title: Curriculum-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robust Autonomous Rocket Landing under Atmospheric Uncertainty
entry.summary: Autonomous far-range rocket landing is a challenging control problem because navigation, descent-rate regulation, attitude management, and fuel use must be coordinated in the presence of uncertain atmospheric and vehicle dynamics. This paper presents a curriculum-driven proximal policy optimization (PPO) framework for three-dimensional rocket landing in a stochastic environment incorporating altitude-dependent aerodynamic drag, wind shear, temporally correlated turbulence, discrete gusts, uncertain propulsion and aerodynamic parameters, thrust-vector misalignment, engine lag, actuator-gain variation, noisy observations, and command latency. Learning is organised into far-range approach, soft descent, and integrated landing stages. Policy transfer, critic warm-up after reward changes, rehearsal of earlier tasks, and progressive expansion of weather severity are used to support learning across these coupled phases. Across 100,000 evaluation episodes, the policy achieves 96,656 successful landings, corresponding to a success rate of 96.656\% and a 95\% Wilson confidence interval of 96.543--96.766\%. Success decreases from 98.84\% under zero-disturbance conditions to 88.07\% in the highest weather-severity band. Successful touchdowns exhibit small miss distances and low residual horizontal and vertical velocities. An exploratory logistic-regression analysis identifies mean wind speed as the strongest measured correlate of success, with initial distance, initial altitude, initial vertical velocity, and wind-shear exponent also associated with outcomes. The results quantify both the effectiveness of the learned policy over the evaluated disturbance distribution and the degradation that occurs under severe compound atmospheric conditions.

entry.title: Lie methods for countably categorical Engel groups: the Wilson conjecture for 4-Engel 5-groups
entry.summary: We are interested in the following conjecture of Wilson from 1981: every locally nilpotent countably categorical group is nilpotent. Following our previous work on the Lie algebra analogue of the conjecture, we use Lie methods to deduce the first nontrivial cases of the Wilson conjecture for n-Engel groups: countably categorical 3-Engel groups and 4-Engel 5-groups are nilpotent, from which we also conclude that countably categorical 4-Engel groups of odd exponent are nilpotent. This is implemented via an exceptional case of the Lazard correspondence, checked using computer algebra systems. We also study the transfer of nilpotency results between the three categories: groups, Lie algebras, associative algebras. Among other things, we prove that the Wilson conjecture implies the analogous nilpotency statement for associative algebras (modulo the commutative case).

entry.title: A Hybrid Physics-informed holomorphic neural networks Method
entry.summary: Physics-informed holomorphic neural networks (PIHNNs) exploit complex-analytic representations to satisfy homogeneous PDEs by construction, but their extension to nonhomogeneous problems is nontrivial. We propose a hybrid physics-informed holomorphic neural network (HPIHNN) framework based on a decomposition of the solution into particular and homogeneous components. The particular component is computed by a spectral method on a simple extended domain, while the homogeneous component is approximated by a PIHNN trained only on the boundary with modified boundary data. The resulting formulation avoids meshing complex geometries and retains the dimensionality-reduction advantage of holomorphic representations. The method is applied to nonhomogeneous Poisson, Stokes, biharmonic, linear elasticity, and Helmholtz equations. Numerical experiments covering complex geometries, corner singularities, and nearly incompressible regimes demonstrate that the proposed method accurately resolves the corresponding solutions and, in the considered tests, generally achieves lower errors and shorter training times than standard PINNs. The results indicate that coupling spectral particular solutions with holomorphic neural approximations provides an efficient approach to nonhomogeneous PDEs on complex domains.

entry.title: LHC di-dijet excesses as signals of fourth-generation tetraquarks
entry.summary: We postulate that the excesses of di-dijet events observed at the LHC are attributed to the production of four fourth-generation quarks $b'$ with a mass $m_{b'}\approx 2$ TeV at few-TeV scales. The di-dijet signals around the four-jet invariant mass $m_{4j}\approx 8$ TeV arise from a resonant $b'b'\bar b'\bar b'$ tetraquark production, where the dijet resonances of masses about 2 TeV correspond to $b'\bar b'$ first excited states (color-octet scalars with the principal quantum number $n=2$) in a Yukawa potential created by Higgs boson exchanges. Those around $m_{4j}\approx 3.6$ TeV originate from a non-resonant $b'b'\bar b'\bar b'$ production, where the dijet resonances of masses 0.95 TeV correspond to $b'\bar b'$ ground states (color-octet vectors with $n=1$). It is shown that a $b'\bar b'$ system with $m_{b'}\approx 2$ TeV in the Yukawa potential does generate the aforementioned bound state spectrum. We then illustrate that the observed excesses can be accommodated in our setup by translating the fourth-generation model to the effective theories containing color-octet scalars and vectors available in the literature. Simply speaking, our scenario can be viewed as a TeV-scale analogue of the search for a fully charmed tetraquark via the four-muon channels $X(6900)\to (c\bar c)(c\bar c)\to 4μ$ at a GeV scale.

entry.title: Unveiling the Shock-Excited Molecular Environment in the Orion Protostar HOPS 370
entry.summary: We present near-infrared K-band ($1.94$--$2.52~μ$m) spectroscopy of the deeply embedded protostellar source HOPS\,370, obtained with the TIFR--ARIES Near Infrared Spectrometer (TANSPEC) on the 3.6-m Devasthal Optical Telescope (DOT). The spectrum is dominated by prominent molecular hydrogen ($\rm H_2$) ro-vibrational emission, with multiple transitions detected from the $1$--$0$ S, $2$--$1$ S, and $1$--$0$ Q branches. Using the intrinsically linked $\rm H_2$ $1$--$0$ Q(3) and $1$--$0$ S(1) transitions, which arise from the same upper energy level, we derive a visual extinction of $A_V = 23.24 \pm 1.25$ mag, corresponding to $A_K = 2.50 \pm 0.13$ mag, consistent with the embedded Class~0/I nature of the source. The diagnostic line ratio $F(2$--$1~{\rm S}(1))/F(1$--$0~{\rm S}(1)) = 0.12 \pm 0.01$ is consistent with thermal excitation and disfavors ultraviolet fluorescence as the dominant excitation mechanism. Assuming optically thin emission and local thermodynamic equilibrium, we derive an $\rm H_2$ excitation diagram that yields an excitation temperature of $2078 \pm 215$ K and a molecular hydrogen column density of $(1.93 \pm 0.93)\times10^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$. We further derive an ortho-to-para ratio of $2.45 \pm 0.21$, indicating substantial shock-driven thermal processing while remaining below the high-temperature equilibrium value of 3. Taken together, these diagnostics indicate that the molecular hydrogen emission in HOPS\,370 originates predominantly in warm, shock-heated gas most likely associated with its protostellar outflow. Our results demonstrate the diagnostic power of combined S- and Q-branch $\rm H_2$ spectroscopy for constraining the physical conditions and excitation history of deeply embedded protostellar systems.

entry.title: Hydration Free Energies from Local Electronic Structures
entry.summary: Free energies of solvation are crucial to our understanding of chemical reactions, particularly when these take place in water. However, computing changes in free energies associated with the process of immersing arbitrary molecules in an aqueous solution both accurately and efficiently with the use of one universal method remains challenging. By means of atomic decompositions of total (bulk) energies from Kohn-Sham density functional theory in a basis of spatially localized molecular orbitals, the present study enables the computation of hydration free energies from local electronic-structure objects derived in the condensed phase. Specifically, our protocol computes an enthalpy of hydration as the sum of the decomposed change in internal energy of a solute upon solvation and a newly developed term that accounts for the response of the environment, which may then be combined with a standard expression for the corresponding change in entropy. In applications to eight neutral solutes in water, internal energies are all found to converge rapidly and in a smooth manner upon an increase in the size of the solvated cluster, and the corresponding enthalpies and free energies of hydration are likewise found to agree with experimental references within statistical uncertainty.

entry.title: Discretisation in algebraic $K$-theory of independent ample groupoids and their Steinberg algebras
entry.summary: An independent ample groupoid $G$ comes equipped with a discrete groupoid $G_d$ and a proper étale correspondence $Ω:G_d\to G$. Discretisation with respect to a homological invariant $\mathcal{H}$ holds when $\mathcal{H}(Ω)$ is an equivalence. We show for example that discretisation with respect to the $K$-theory spectrum $\mathbb{K} \mathfrak{B}_G$ of the permutative category of bisections always holds, establish excision and continuity for this invariant, and use all this and explicit resolutions by independent groupoids to compute it for several families of ample groupoids. We also prove discretisation with respect to invariants of the Steinberg algebra $\ell[G]$ such as (homotopy) algebraic $K$-theory in several particular cases, and carry out computations.

entry.title: Predicting $B^{(*)}\bar D{}^{(*)}$ states from a reanalysis of lattice QCD data
entry.summary: We reanalyze the lattice QCD data for the isoscalar $\bar b\bar c ud$ systems with $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ at $m_π\simeq 220$ MeV, incorporating both short- and long-range interactions constrained by heavy-quark spin and chiral symmetries. Using the interaction fitted to the lattice results, we predict a spectrum of isoscalar $B^{(*)}\bar D{}^{(*)}$ molecular states with quantum numbers $J^P=0^+$, $1^+$, and $2^+$. The predicted $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ $B\bar D$ and $B^*\bar D$ bound states are consistent with the lattice results. Furthermore, the two resonances reported by the lattice collaboration in the $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ $\bar b\bar c ud$ channels can be naturally interpreted as $B^*\bar D{}^*$ and $B\bar D{}^*$ hadronic molecules, respectively. We also predict two previously unreported $B^*\bar D{}^*$ states with $J^P=1^+$ and $2^+$: a bound state and a shallow state whose pole may correspond to either a virtual state or a bound state, respectively. Our results provide a unified interpretation of the lattice spectrum and highlight the interplay between short- and long-range interactions in the dynamics of the $B^{(*)}\bar D{}^{(*)}$ systems.

entry.title: On The Scaling Relations Between Black Holes And The Galaxy/Bulge Mass And Their Connections With The Black Hole Occupation Fraction
entry.summary: We investigate the black hole (BH)--host galaxy scaling relations predicted by the semianalytic model \texttt{FEGA25}, focusing on their dependence on BH mass threshold, galaxy morphology, and redshift, and on their connection with the BH occupation fraction (BHOF). Using the YS200 cosmological simulation as our reference volume, we study the $M_{\rm BH}$--$M_{\star}$ and $M_{\rm BH}$--$M_{\rm bulge}$ relations for different BH mass selections and compare their redshift evolution with the hydrodynamical zoom-in simulation \texttt{NewCluster}. We find that BH mass cuts primarily affect the low-mass regime, while the selected relations progressively converge toward the intrinsic no-cut relations at higher host masses. The $M_{\rm BH}$--$M_{\star}$ relation also depends systematically on galaxy morphology, with increasingly bulge-dominated systems preferentially occupying higher stellar masses. Over $z=0$--$3$, FEGA25 shows no clear systematic evolution of either scaling relation, consistent with a broadly preserved statistical connection between BH and host-galaxy growth. NewCluster shows no clear monotonic evolution either, although it exhibits larger scatter, particularly toward high host masses. We further show that BHOF and BH--host scaling relations encode complementary information. A low BHOF generally corresponds to a stronger selection-induced offset, but the mapping is not unique: substantially different occupation fractions can yield similar median scaling relations, and at fixed BHOF the bias depends on the host property and underlying BH mass distribution. At $z=0$, \texttt{FEGA25} is consistent with available observational constraints for both stellar- and bulge-mass relations, while predicting increased scatter and bending toward lower host masses.

entry.title: Gravitational field of spinors with torsion and matter$-$antimatter asymmetry
entry.summary: The conservation law for the orbital plus spin angular momentum of a free Dirac particle in curved spacetime requires that the affine connection has the antisymmetric part: the torsion tensor, which extends general relativity to the Einstein$-$Cartan theory of gravity. In spacetime with torsion, the Dirac equation becomes a nonlinear, cubic equation in the spinor wave function. Under charge conjugation, the nonlinear term changes sign relative to the mass term. A Dirac spinor and its charge conjugate therefore satisfy different field equations. We use the spinor connection formalism to derive the Dirac equation for a spherical spinor in its centrally symmetric gravitational field with torsion. We determine the energy$-$momentum tensor for this spinor and show that the energy contribution from torsion is negative for matter particles and positive for antimatter particles. Consequently, the ground state of a fermion has a lower energy than the ground state of the corresponding antifermion. We also derive the Einstein$-$Cartan$-$Dirac equations for this spinor; they indicate the existence of particle-like soliton solutions exhibiting matter$-$antimatter energy asymmetry.

entry.title: Graphon Colourings and Limits of Graph Partitions
entry.summary: We develop a framework for pure and mixed graphon colourings and use it to study the limiting behaviour of graph partition parameters under cut convergence. Pure colourings correspond to measurable partitions, while mixed colourings assign a probability distribution on the colour set to each point. We develop the representation, equivalence and convergence theory, and show that every mixed graphon colouring has an equivalent pure representative, possibly on a different probability space. For each fixed finite colour set, we establish compactness and describe the topology of coloured graph limits using the cut norm on graphons and the weak-$*$ topology on colourings. The usual coloured cut distance characterises convergence for pure colourings, but not for general mixed colourings. As applications, we prove that the Cheeger constant and modularity converge to their mixed graphon counterparts along cut-convergent graph sequences whose orders tend to infinity, assuming uniformly linear minimum degree and positive limiting edge density, respectively. Both mixed functionals are invariant under graphon equivalence. We also establish their continuity in cut distance on the corresponding classes of graphons, with a stability bound for the Cheeger constant. For modularity, we further characterise coloured graphons attaining extremal modularity values and prove attainment of the mixed optimum for each fixed number of colours. We also exhibit a graphon whose modularity supremum is not attained by any finite colouring.

entry.title: Game-Theoretic Foundations for Undiscounted Bisimulation Metrics
entry.summary: Bisimulation metrics offer a principled notion of task-relevant state similarity in reinforcement learning, but existing constructions and methods are largely confined to discounted MDPs, where contraction arguments ensure well-defined fixed points and downstream guarantees. We develop a unified foundation for bisimulation metrics in undiscounted settings, that is total- and average-reward problems, by replacing the standard operator-centric view with a game-centric one: we interpret prior metric operators as Bellman-Shapley operators of zero-sum turn-based games and define metrics as the corresponding game value functions, yielding unique definitions even when $γ=1$. This game-theoretic foundation facilitates transfer of dynamic-programming theory and algorithms. We also use this game-centric perspective to characterize how metric finiteness depends on structural properties of the underlying MDP and motivate certain directed metrics that remain finite in weakly communicating MDPs. We further introduce an abstract framework for modifying the games' action spaces, allowing general transition coupling sets, that recovers many existing metrics and guides new constructions. Finally, we prove that these metrics bound total-reward and, when the optimal gain is state-independent, optimal relative value differences. We also provide error and suboptimality guarantees for aggregation-based planning in total- and average-reward settings.

entry.title: Quasi-Trefftz spaces for a second order time-harmonic Maxwell's equation
entry.summary: Quasi-Trefftz methods are a family of Discontinuous Galerkin methods relying on equation-dependent function spaces. This work is the first study of the notion of local Taylor-based polynomial quasi-Trefftz spaces for a system of Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). These discrete spaces are meant to discretize a quasi-Trefftz weak formulation, and are introduced here for electro-magnetic wave propagation in inhomogeneous media, governed by a second order formulation of Maxwell's equation with variable coefficients. Thanks to an adequate Helmholtz decomposition for spaces of homogeneous polynomial vector fields, the outcome is the proposed quasi-Trefftz spaces with same best approximation properties as the corresponding standard polynomial spaces but with an optimal dimension, as well as a procedure to construct a quasi-Trefftz basis.

entry.title: Convergence analysis of an augmented dual-mixed fnite element method with skew-symmetric Nitsche stabilization for the generalized Oseen equations with mixed boundary conditions
entry.summary: In this paper, we propose and analyze a new skew-symmetric Nitsche-augmented mixed scheme for the generalized Oseen equations with non-solenoidal convective fields, subject to mixed boundary conditions. The scheme is based on a continuous pseudostress-velocity augmented dual-mixed finite element formulation, in which the Dirichlet datum is imposed naturally, whereas the prescribed normal trace of the pseudostress is incorporated into the $H(div,)$ stress space. We establish the well-posedness of the continuous formulation by means of a classical lifting argument and its corresponding homogeneous problem. The essential boundary condition is then weakly enforced in the discrete scheme through suitable stabilizing Nitsche terms. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution to the discrete scheme, allowing the use of general conforming approximation spaces for both the pseudostress and the velocity. Moreover, in the case of homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and general Neumann data, we establish the stability of the Nitsche scheme. Under mild regularity assumptions on the exact solution, we prove optimal convergence rates in an energy norm. Finally, numerical experiments in two and three dimensions confirm the theoretical convergence rates and assess the performance of the proposed scheme for non-solenoidal convective fields and solutions exhibiting boundary layers.

entry.title: Equal diffusions and zero Dirichlet boundary conditions can induce blow-up
entry.summary: For a class of systems of two parabolic equations with equal diffusion and homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, we show the existence of finite time blow-up solutions, although the corresponding system of ODE's has only global, exponentially decaying solutions. Such a phenomenon of blow-up induced by equal diffusions, which originates in the works of Bebernes-Lacey [SIAM J. Math. Anal. 21 (1990), 1415--1425, and J. Differential Equations 95 (1992), 105--129] and Weinberger [J. Differ. Equations 154 (1999), 225--237], was previously known, for instance, in the case of homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, but it had remained an open question whether it can happen in the homogeneous Dirichlet case. The latter, which corresponds to an absorption or cooling of the system at the boundary, that is a priori more stabilizing, requires nontrivial new ideas. As another new feature, we show that this can happen even if the nonlinearity acts only on a compact sub-region, and our proof actually covers the Neumann and Cauchy, as well as Dirichlet problems in a unified way.

entry.title: High-dimensional two-sample testing: From optimal transport to optimal derangements
entry.summary: In recent years, optimal transport has emerged as a useful framework for constructing distribution-free multivariate two-sample tests by transporting observations to a reference distribution under a suitable transportation cost. However, existing optimal transport-based tests can perform poorly in high dimension, low sample size (HDLSS) settings, and their performance depends critically on the choice of the reference distribution and transportation cost. We investigate this phenomenon and show that suitable choices can substantially improve their performance. Motivated by this analysis, we introduce a class of two-sample tests based on optimal derangements that do not require an external reference distribution. The minimum distance pairing test of Rosenbaum arises as a special case when the optimization is restricted to a subclass of derangements, thereby revealing a connection between this method and optimal transport. We propose the optimal derangement (ODER) test and its distribution-free variant, the ODER-SHC test, obtained by restricting the minimization to derangements consisting of a single Hamiltonian cycle. We establish their consistency under both HDLSS and classical large-sample asymptotic regimes. We also develop corresponding procedures based on the $L1$ distance and establish their high-dimensional consistency under conditions involving coordinate-wise energy distances. These $L1$ distance based tests can also discriminate between two high-dimensional distributions with identical first two moments but different marginal distributions. Analyses of benchmark datasets and extensive simulation studies demonstrate the performance of the proposed methods across a variety of alternatives and data settings.

entry.title: Reciprocal transverse Seebeck and Peltier effects in MoSi2
entry.summary: Transverse thermoelectric conversion, in which charge and heat currents are interconverted in orthogonal directions, has recently attracted increasing attention as an alternative to conventional longitudinal thermoelectric conversion. Although transverse Seebeck effect has been investigated in various materials, its reciprocal process, transverse Peltier effect, remains much less explored, and direct comparison of the two effects in the same homogeneous material is still limited. Here, we experimentally investigate both transverse Seebeck and Peltier effects in a single crystal of MoSi2, an axis-dependent conduction polarity material in which the sign of the Seebeck coefficient varies depending on the crystallographic axis. Multi-terminal voltage measurement determines the direction of the induced internal electric field and establishes the transverse Seebeck response. We also directly visualize the transverse temperature modulation consistent with the corresponding transverse Peltier effect by using lock-in thermography under an applied ac current. These results establish reciprocal transverse thermoelectric conversion in a homogeneous nonmagnetic single crystal without engineered interfaces.

entry.title: Gluon gravitational form factors of the proton from near-threshold charmonium photoproduction
entry.summary: Motivated by near-threshold $J/ψ$ photoproduction measurements, we investigate the gluon contributions to the gravitational form factors (GFFs) of the proton associated with the energy-momentum tensor in quantum chromodynamics. We calculate the gluon GFFs and the corresponding mechanical properties of the proton within a light-front spectator model, in which the proton is described as an active gluon accompanied by a spectator particle. The model parameters are determined from a global fit to the differential cross section for $J/ψ$ photoproduction. The resulting gluon GFFs are in reasonable agreement with recent lattice QCD determinations. We further calculate the total cross section and find reasonable agreement with the available experimental data. Using the extracted gluon GFFs, we investigate the two-dimensional light-front gluon distributions inside the proton, such as the mass, angular momentum, pressure, and shear force distributions. We also study the gluonic contributions to the two-dimensional Galilean energy density, radial and tangential pressures, isotropic pressure, and pressure anisotropy.

entry.title: Tensor products of 2-representations
entry.summary: In this paper we define comonoidal structures on additive $\Bbbk$-linear $2$-categories which guarantee the existence of a monoidal structure on the corresponding $2$-categories of $2$-representations.

entry.title: Fractal dimension of singular times for SPDEs: Energy bounds, criticality, and weak-strong uniqueness
entry.summary: For several physically relevant SPDEs, it is known that global weak solutions coexist with local strong ones. Typically, weak-strong uniqueness results are known, and ensure that the global and strong solutions coincide as long as the latter exist. Times at which a weak solution does not coincide with a strong one are called singular times. Determining their fractal dimension is fundamental to capturing the regularity of weak solutions. We introduce a probabilistic notion of singular times for a wide class of semilinear SPDEs. We show that sets of singular times have fractal dimension (i.e., Hausdorff and/or Minkowski) at most $ 1-\ell\, \mathsf{Exc}$, where $\ell$ and $\mathsf{Exc}$ are the time integrability and the excess of spatial regularity compared to the critical regularity of the energy bound associated with weak solutions, respectively. Moreover, their corresponding $(1-\ell\,\mathsf{Exc} )$-dimensional measure is zero. We formulate and apply our theory to annealed strong Leray-Hopf solutions of 3D Navier-Stokes equations (NSEs) with physically relevant noises, including rough Kraichnan and Lie transport. In particular, we extend the fundamental $1/2$-dimensional bound of Leray and Scheffer on singular times for 3D NSEs to the stochastic setting, and we prove new conditional results under supercritical Serrin's conditions, irrespective of the roughness of the noise. Our framework is new even in the deterministic case, and provides the first partial regularity results for weak solutions to SPDEs with multiplicative noise.

entry.title: Spectral-Aligned Pruning for Universal Error-Correcting Code Transformers
entry.summary: Universal channel decoders based on transformers-such as the Foundation Error Correction Code Transformer (FECCT)-achieve competitive decoding performance across diverse code families with a single shared backbone, optionally followed by code-specific finetuning. However, the high computational complexity and large parameter footprint of FECCT present substantial obstacles to practical deployment. To address these challenges, we investigate structured pruning for FECCT and propose Spectral-Aligned Pruning (SAP), a structure-aware framework that enables cross-code reuse of structured pruning masks by leveraging the spectrum of the corresponding bipartite graph. SAP is grounded in classical graph analysis of codes: the two algebraically largest adjacency eigenvalues provide compact spectral proxies for degree scale, expansion ratio, and minimum-distance lower bounds. These quantities are directly relevant to decoding performance: degree scale reflects how densely codeword bits and parity checks are connected; expansion ratio influences how information propagates across the bipartite graph; and minimum distance characterizes codeword separation. Based on this connection, SAP uses these two leading eigenvalues as a lightweight code signature for pruning-mask retrieval. Empirically, this two-dimensional signature yields stable library selection equivalent to higher-dimensional spectral signatures in our evaluation. After pruning, SAP uses parameter-efficient low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to recover decoding performance while storing only a small number of additional adapter parameters per code. Experiments across diverse codes show that SAP achieves decoding performance comparable to dedicated per-code pruning, while enabling substantial reductions in computational cost and model memory footprint through kernel-level structured pruning. Code is available at https://github.com/iil-postech/sap.

entry.title: Maximizing R{é}nyi Entropy over the Transportation Polytope: Structure and Algorithm
entry.summary: We study the problem of finding the minimum $\mathbb{L}\_2$-norm element in a transportation polytope. It corresponds to minimizing the index of coincidence or maximizing R{é}nyi entropy over joint probability distributions with prescribed marginals. The solution is straightforward under a feasibility condition on the marginals. We make three contributions. First, we decompose the basic solution into a mixture of three interpretable couplings and derive a closed-form sampling procedure, revealing its role as the $\mathbb{L}\_2$-projection of the uniform distribution onto the transportation polytope. Second, we show that the feasibility condition becomes exponentially rare as the number of modalities grows, which highlights the practical necessity of a more general construction. Third, we provide a KKT-based iterative construction of the optimal coupling for arbitrary marginals with explicit Lagrange multipliers.

entry.title: From pq-webs to magnetic quivers and back I: dictionary and deformations
entry.summary: This is the first of two companion papers in which we study five-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories engineered by $(p,q)$ five-brane webs and their associated three-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=4$ magnetic quivers. We focus on the $N+\mathrm{SU}(N)_0^{k-1}+N$ box quiver theories. We propose an exact parameter dictionary relating the five-dimensional flavour masses and instanton couplings to the Fayet-Iliopoulos parameters of the corresponding strong-coupling magnetic quiver. We test this dictionary through a broad class of deformations, including mass deformations, weak-coupling limits, and vacuum expectation values. On the five-dimensional side, we implement these flows directly at the level of the superconformal index. The dictionary fixes the corresponding FI deformations and monopole VEVs. We analyse them in the magnetic-quiver squashed-sphere partition function using a new method that tracks Higgsing, decoupled sectors, and infrared theories. Our results promote magnetic quivers to tools for the quantitative study of how the five-dimensional superconformal index responds to deformations. Once the parameter dictionary is known, exact three-dimensional observables can be used to reconstruct the corresponding five-dimensional physics and to navigate the full deformation network in both directions.

entry.title: Uniqueness and radial nondegeneracy of nodal states for a mixed-power scalar field equation
entry.summary: We consider the scalar field equation $$\begin{cases} -Δu+u+λ|u|^{q-1}u =μ|u|^{p-1}u, & x\in\mathbb R^n,\\[2mm] u(x)\to 0, & |x|\to\infty, \end{cases}$$ where $n\geq3$, $1<q<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, and $λ,μ>0$. We study uniqueness and radial nondegeneracy of its sign-changing radial bound states. The proof combines a comparison argument for the shooting variation across nodal intervals with uniform compactness estimates for families of bounded nodal number and continuation in a normalized parameter. We show that, for every integer $k\geq1$, fixing the centre and requiring $u(0)>0$ leaves exactly one radial bound state with $k$ nodes. Its radial linearized operator has trivial kernel in the radial space. For each fixed $k$, the corresponding normalized solutions form a global $C^1$ branch.

entry.title: Optimal Regret for Communication-Efficient Decentralized Online Learning
entry.summary: In this paper, we investigate decentralized online convex optimization with compressed communication, where $n$ learners over a network jointly minimize a sequence of global loss functions based only on their local losses and compressed messages from their neighbors. The best known regret bounds for this problem are $O(ω^{-1/2}nρ^{-1}\sqrt{T\ln n})$ and $O(ω^{-1}nρ^{-2}\ln n\ln T)$ for convex and strongly convex loss functions, respectively, where $ρ\in(0,1)$ is the spectral gap of the communication matrix and $ω\in(0,1]$ is the compression quality factor. Compared with the corresponding lower bounds of $Ω(ω^{-1/2}nρ^{-1/4}\sqrt{T})$ and $Ω(ω^{-1}nρ^{-1/2}\ln T)$, these upper bounds exhibit polynomial gaps in their dependence on $ρ^{-1}$. To close these gaps, we first develop Ascent-gossip, which combines an online compression strategy with a Chebyshev recursion and attains a faster consensus rate than existing compressed gossip methods. Furthermore, by adopting Ascent-gossip, we propose an online algorithm that achieves optimal regret bounds of $\widetilde O(ω^{-1/2}nρ^{-1/4}\sqrt{T})$ and $\widetilde O(ω^{-1}nρ^{-1/2}\ln T)$ for convex and strongly convex loss functions, respectively. Up to logarithmic factors in $n$ and $ρ^{-1}$, these results match the lower bounds in terms of $T$, $n$, $ρ$, and $ω$.

entry.title: Strict Frequency Bandwidths from Causal Light Cones Enable Scalable Exact Gradient Evaluation in Quantum Optimization
entry.summary: Dynamical locality is often regarded as a limitation of shallow quantum circuits, yet we show that it can reduce the number of circuit settings required for exact evaluation of gradients with respect to shared parameters. For layered ansatze generated by commuting local terms, strict Heisenberg light cones confine energy slices obtained by varying one shared layer parameter to finite Fourier bandwidths dictated by local causal geometry. This bandlimit recasts exact gradient evaluation as a local signal recovery problem and, when the relevant frequencies lie on a known frequency lattice, yields an exact multipoint parameter-shift rule based on the discrete sine transform. The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) provides a canonical realization in which this mechanism is governed by the local structure of the graph. Specifically, when a cost angle is varied, the relevant geometry is encoded by the contact region in the interaction line graph. At fixed circuit depth on graphs of bounded degree, the number of distinct circuit settings required for the corresponding derivative collapses from $O(m)$ to $O(1)$. This shows that dynamical locality is not merely a constraint on correlation propagation, but also a computational resource that enables exact gradient evaluation with fewer circuit settings in quantum optimization.

entry.title: Energy Estimate and Convergence of Weak Solutions of a Class of Nonlinear PDEs with Robin Boundary Conditions
entry.summary: We establish strong convergence in $L^2([0,T]\times[0,1])$ of weak solutions to a class of nonlinear PDEs with Robin boundary conditions to weak solutions of the corresponding Neumann and Dirichlet problems as the boundary parameter $κ$ tends to $0$ and $\infty$, respectively. Our approach relies on a particle system whose hydrodynamic limits yield the Robin problem for each fixed $κ>0$. An energy estimate derived from the microscopic stochastic dynamics provides the key bounds for passing to the subsequent limits $κ\to0$ and $κ\to\infty$, thereby obtaining the Neumann and Dirichlet problems.

entry.title: Minimum-Time Trajectory for Escort-Assisted Evasion from a Sensing-Limited Pursuer
entry.summary: This paper studies a minimum-time path-planning problem in which an escort assists a leader by triggering and redirecting a sensing-limited pursuer. For the post-engagement case with equal leader, escort, and pursuer speeds, we show that the minimum-time leader trajectory has a three-phase structure: an initial straight segment, a moving-boundary segment, and a final straight segment to the goal. The boundary-following kinematics and the corresponding entry and exit conditions are derived and used to construct the leader trajectory for a fixed escort engagement direction. The engagement direction is then optimized over the feasible set to obtain the minimum-time solution. Numerical results illustrate the resulting trajectory and the benefits of escort assistance.

entry.title: Finite-State Time-Inhomogeneous Markov Chains Conditioned to Survive
entry.summary: We study conditioning on long survival for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains on finite state spaces. We assume that a sequence of substochastic transition kernels converges to an irreducible substochastic kernel and that the transition probabilities admit asymptotic expansions up to order $n^{-2}$. Under these assumptions, we construct a positive space-time harmonic function and prove that the limiting path distributions under conditioning on long survival are given by the corresponding Doob h-transform. We also investigate the long-time behavior of the resulting conditioned process. Finally, we apply our general theory to an elephant random walk, a generalized Pólya urn model, time-inhomogeneous Wright--Fisher and Moran models, and noncolliding random walks.

entry.title: Beyond Fresnel Approximation: Exact Airy Beamforming for Near-Field THz Communications
entry.summary: Line-of-sight (LoS) blockage can severely degrade the performance of conventional focused beams in terahertz (THz) communications. Recently, bending beams (e.g., Airy beams) have attracted increasing attention due to their ability to bypass obstacles by propagating along curved trajectories under near-field propagation conditions. However, existing Airy-beam designs in wireless communications often rely on the Fresnel approximation for the focal distance, which becomes inaccurate at large steering angles or short propagation distances. To address this limitation, this letter proposes a more accurate Airy beamforming design method based on the exact focal-distance expression and the corresponding caustic geometry. Specifically, we jointly optimize the bending curvature, virtual focal distance, and steering angle to maximize the received signal power subject to receiver-alignment and obstacle-avoidance constraints. To tackle the resulting non-convex problem, we first use geometric preprocessing to narrow the feasible range of the bending curvature. Then, a two-layer optimization framework is developed with the outer and inner layers optimizing the bending curvature and the other two parameters, respectively. Numerical results based on the cascaded geometrical and wave channel model demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher received signal power than conventional Airy-beam designs and offers complementary advantages over conventional focused beams under different blockage ratios.

entry.title: Tracing Electromagnetic Response through Charge Splitting of Directed Flow in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
entry.summary: Experimentally observed charge splitting of directed flow, $Δv_1\equiv v_1(h^+)-v_1(h^-)$, exhibits both a sign reversal at midrapidity and the amplitude change from Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV to Pb+Pb at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.02$ TeV. We study this behavior within a unified $(3+1)$-dimensional viscous hydrodynamic model that incorporates an electromagnetic source term in the bulk evolution of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) and an electromagnetic correction to the Cooper--Frye particlization. The beam-energy dependence of $Δv_1$ can be described by varying the effective electrical conductivity between RHIC and LHC energies, with values consistent with the conductivity scale indicated by lattice-QCD calculations. We find that the sign reversal emerges from the competition between momentum distortions induced by the electric and magnetic field which is controlled by the conductivity during the QGP evolution. The model further predicts the mass-dependent charge splittings for identified pions, kaons, and protons, providing further constraints on their respective relaxation times and the corresponding electromagnetic interaction. These results establish the charge splitting of directed flow as a quantitative probe of the electromagnetic response and the space-time evolution of the QGP.

entry.title: DRC-TTS: A Dual-Resolution Codec-Based Architecture for Lexicon-Free Malay Speech Synthesis
entry.summary: Modern discrete neural audio codecs facilitate speech synthesis by replacing continuous acoustic representations with low-frame-rate discrete token sequences. For Malay speech synthesis, character-level input reduces reliance on pronunciation lexicons. However, combining character-level inputs with low-frame-rate discrete codecs introduces a temporal alignment challenge. When predicted character durations are quantized into frame counts at 12.5 Hz, durations shorter than one codec frame may be assigned zero frames. Consequently, the corresponding character representations may be lost during length regulation, potentially leading to pronunciation omissions. This study proposes DRC-TTS, a dual-resolution codec-based architecture for lexicon-free Malay speech synthesis. The model expands character representations at a temporal resolution of 50 Hz and subsequently downsamples them through strided convolution to 12.5 Hz for discrete codec-token prediction. Objective evaluations show that the proposed model reduces the character error rate (CER) from 27.11% for the baseline to 21.86%, an absolute reduction of 5.25 percentage points. The proposed model also achieves a mean opinion score (MOS) of 4.30, compared with 4.12 for the baseline. These results suggest that the dual-resolution design may improve character-level alignment and perceived speech naturalness under the evaluated conditions.

entry.title: A Witnessing Duality for ReLU Network Depth
entry.summary: A depth lower bound for ReLU networks asserts that every shallower network errs on some input; we ask when a weak theory can prove such a bound so that an error can be computed. For the exact computation of $\max(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$, recent work shows two hidden layers suffice with unrestricted rational weights. By contrast, Haase, Hertrich and Loho (ICLR 2023) proved that integer weights require depth logarithmic in $n$, and Averkov, Hojny and Merkert (ICLR 2025) extended the bound to nonbias weights whose denominators are powers of a fixed integer not divisible by a prime $q$. With integer weights the bound is sharp: the classical balanced construction has depth $\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$. For each fixed $q$ and depth cap $K$, we prove this known bound in $\mathbf{VTC}^0$, the bounded-arithmetic theory of uniform constant-depth threshold computation, together with a refuter that is itself such a computation and whose correctness the theory proves. Given a network with at most $K$ hidden layers, nonbias weights whose reduced denominators avoid $q$, arbitrary rational biases and $n>q^K$ inputs, the refuter returns a rational input of polynomial length on which the network errs. The proof makes the obstruction finite: an iterated intersection product of piecewise-linear functions is divisible by $q$ for the network but not for the maximum, so one of finitely many test points exposes the error. By witnessing, provable refutation corresponds to a provably correct refuter, and provable existence of a certified network to a provably correct constructor. On the construction side, we introduce certificates that label each maximum gadget by the inputs it aggregates; with them the theory verifies the balanced construction, which meets the refuter at the sharp threshold $n\le2^K$, and a rational family of polynomial description length and depth $O(\log n/\log\log n)$ built from known depth-two blocks.

entry.title: Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin methods for the Keller-Segel model
entry.summary: We propose a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) finite element method to approximate the solution of the time-dependent Keller-Segel model, a drift-diffusion system describing chemotactic cell movement. We develop and analyze the corresponding HDG scheme, and establish theoretical convergence results for the proposed discretization. Finally, we present numerical experiments that confirm the theoretical findings.

entry.title: Benchmarking Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials for Temperature-Dependent Elasticity of Binary and High-Entropy Refractory Carbides
entry.summary: Accurate predictions of temperature-dependent stiffness are essential for assessing the high-temperature performance of refractory carbides, yet the cost of ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) limits systematic exploration across compositions and temperatures. Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) offer a computationally efficient alternative, but their reliability for finite-temperature elasticity remains insufficiently established. Here, we benchmark nine uMLIPs against consistent AIMD reference data for five binary and two high-entropy (HE) carbides between 300 and 1200 K. Elastic constants and the corresponding bulk, shear, and Young's moduli are obtained using stress-strain molecular dynamics, explicitly sampling thermal atomic motion and anharmonic effects beyond thermal expansion alone. We assess absolute elastic properties and normalized thermal softening separately. MACE-MH-1 achieves the lowest overall mean absolute percentage error (5.7%). MACE-MH-1 and DPA4-Mini reproduce thermal softening most accurately, with mean deviations of 2.5 and 2.3 percentage points, respectively. All models generally underestimate stiffness, with larger equilibrium volumes relative to the AIMD reference likely contributing to this trend for most models. C12 exhibits the largest model-dependent errors. The HE carbides are described with accuracy comparable to that of the binary carbides, indicating no apparent accuracy penalty from chemical complexity. Accuracy instead varies with transition-metal composition, with group-V carbides, particularly TaC, presenting the greatest challenge. These results identify promising pretrained models for finite-temperature elasticity in carbides and show why accurate absolute stiffness and thermal softening must be assessed independently.

entry.title: Local geometry for Schmidt number witnesses
entry.summary: Suppose that $F_E$ is the face of the convex set of all $m\otimes n$ bi-partite states which consists of states with ranges contained in a subspace $E$. By the result in [Phys. Rev. A {\bf 112} (2025), 032426], there exist Schmidt number $\ell$ witnesses outside of the face $F_{E^\perp}$ if and only if $\ell\leμ$, where $μ$ is the minimum of Schmidt ranks of nonzero vectors in $E$. In this paper, we show that every neighborhood of the projection state located at the center of $F_{E^\perp}$ contains Schmidt number $\ell$ witnesses if and only if $\ell\geμ$. In order to understand the local shape of the convex sets of $k$-blockpositive matrices around this projection state, we introduce principal supporting hyperplanes, and show that they correspond to vectors in $E$ with Schmidt rank $\le k$. Using techniques from algebraic geometry, we show that the inclusions between these convex sets are detected by principal supporting hyperplanes through the projection state for generic subspaces $E$, while for non-generic subspaces they may not be detected by any supporting hyperplane.

entry.title: Vacancy Effect on the Ground-State Energy of a Bose Gas Trapped by 1D Imperfect Artificial Crystal
entry.summary: For a weakly interacting Bose gas trapped by an imperfect one-dimensional artificial crystal, we study the effect of its punctual defects, i.e. vacancies, on the ground state properties of the system. In the framework of the mean field approximation, we numerically solve the corresponding Gross-Pitaevskii equation using the ``Gradient Flow with Discrete Normalization'' method, also known as the imaginary time method. The crystal is artificially produced by applying an external Dirac comb potential to the Bose gas where vacancies are created by randomly removing a predetermined number of deltas. We observe that as the number of randomly removed deltas increases, the ground state energy decreases exponentially from its value for the perfect crystal case until it reaches its value when the Bose gas is free. The ground state energy is reported for different magnitudes of the interaction between bosons and several system sizes which we extrapolate to infinity for the crystal with only one vacancy. Also, we observe the presence of an energy gap between the ground state energies of the perfect system and that with a vacancy, which is more noticeable for values of the particle interaction magnitude $ g \leq 0.1$, when the delta strength $P_0 = 10$. In addition, we report the boson distributions within the crystal, %inside a box with periodic boundary conditions, i.e. the probability density functions which show localization features around vacancies which disappear as $g$ increases. From the ground state energy, the chemical potential is obtained immediately.

entry.title: ECG-Reasoning-Benchmark: A Benchmark for Evaluating Clinical Reasoning Capabilities in ECG Interpretation
entry.summary: While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) show promising performance in automated electrocardiogram interpretation, it remains unclear whether they perform actual step-by-step reasoning or just rely on superficial visual cues. To investigate this, we introduce ECG-Reasoning-Benchmark, a novel multi-turn evaluation framework comprising over 6,400 samples to systematically assess step- by-step reasoning across 17 core ECG diagnoses. Our comprehensive evaluation of state-of-the-art models reveals a systematic shortfall in executing multi-step logical deduction. Although models possess the medical knowledge to retrieve clinical criteria for a diagnosis, they exhibit consistently low success rates in maintaining a complete reasoning chain, primarily failing to ground the corresponding ECG findings to the actual visual evidence in the ECG signal. These results demonstrate that current MLLMs bypass actual visual interpretation, highlighting a limitation in their visual grounding capabilities and motivating robust, reasoning-centric medical AI. The code and data are available at https://github.com/Jwoo5/ecg-reasoning-benchmark.

entry.title: Regge trajectories from the adjoint sector of Matrix Quantum Mechanics
entry.summary: We reexamine the large $N$ limit of SU$(N)$ symmetric quantum mechanics of a Hermitian matrix whose singlet sector is well known to be exactly solvable via free fermions. When the Fermi level approaches a maximum of the potential, there is critical behavior corresponding to string theory in two dimensions. We uncover new phenomena in the adjoint sector by solving the Marchesini-Onofri equation both numerically and analytically using semiclassical approximations: at criticality, the spectrum is governed by Regge trajectories with energy eigenvalues growing according to $Δ^2 \sim n/ α'$. In the dual 2D string theory, we interpret these states as oscillatory excitations of a ``short'' folded open string. Up to sub-leading corrections, this Regge behavior is essentially universal and is insensitive to the particular potential we choose to approach criticality. Slightly away from criticality, the highly excited states transition into ``long strings'' that extend far into the Liouville direction.

entry.title: Global Well-Posedness of the Vacuum Free Boundary Problem for the Degenerate Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations With Large Data of Spherical Symmetry
entry.summary: The study of global-in-time dynamics of vacuum is crucial for understanding viscous flows. In particular, physical vacuum, which ensures a finite, nontrivial pressure-induced acceleration in the normal direction on the moving boundary, naturally arises in the motion of gaseous stars and shallow water. The corresponding large-data problems for spherically symmetric flows remain open, due to the combined difficulties of coordinate singularity at the origin and degeneracy on the moving boundary. In this paper, we analyze the free boundary problem for the barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with density-dependent viscosity coefficients (as in the shallow water equations) in two and three spatial dimensions. For a general class of spherically symmetric initial densities: $ρ_0^β\in H^3$ with $β\in (\frac{1}{3},γ-1]$ ($γ$: adiabatic exponent), vanishing on the moving boundary in the form of a distance function, we establish the global existence of the unique classical solution with large data. Moreover, our solution is classical up to the moving boundary, and the physical vacuum is allowed for the data under consideration here when $β=γ-1$. The key ingredient of our analysis is to obtain the uniform control over the first-order spatial derivatives of the flow map $η(t,r)$ in spherically symmetric Lagrangian coordinates, which is achieved by some novel density-weighted estimates and flow-map-weighted estimates for the solutions.

entry.title: Archimedean Asai Zeta Integrals and Cohomological Test Vectors
entry.summary: We construct explicit test vectors in the minimal $U(n)$-types of cohomological principal series representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb C)$, together with Schwartz functions, for which the Flicker zeta integrals equal the corresponding Asai $L$-factors. Both the vectors and the Schwartz functions are independent of $s$, with all normalization constants given explicitly. We construct the vectors through a polynomial realization of Schur modules. Schur orthogonality reduces the Flicker integrals to Mellin transforms of Whittaker functions, and Godement sections yield a recurrence for their Jacquet integrals. The lower-rank vectors depend on the remaining integration variables, preventing a direct reduction to lower-rank Flicker integrals. We overcome this difficulty by combining growth estimates derived from the recurrence with the Asai functional equation. This proves that the holomorphic quotient of the Flicker integral by its Asai $L$-factor is constant. An explicit asymptotic calculation shows that this constant is exactly one.

entry.title: Geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack
entry.summary: The analytic Emerton-Gee stack is a rigid analytic moduli stack of $(\varphi,Γ)$-modules over the Robba ring, and is expected to play a fundamental role in the categorical $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence for locally analytic representations. In this paper, we establish the fundamental geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack: it is a rigid analytic Artin stack, normal, a local complete intersection, and equidimensional of the expected dimension. As an application, our normality result removes the reducedness hypothesis in the paper of Le, Strauch, and Wang, thereby yielding an unconditional proof of the conjecture on the global sections of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack formulated by Emerton, Gee, and Hellmann.

entry.title: New Explicit Examples of Mannheim Pairs in $\mathbb{R}^3$
entry.summary: In this paper, we construct new explicit parametrizations of Mannheim pairs in Euclidean 3-space. Unlike the known examples in the literature, which are essentially slant helices or general helices, the curve presented here is neither a helix nor a slant helix. We provide the full Frenet apparatus, the explicit Cartesian coordinates expressed in terms of elementary functions, and the corresponding Mannheim partner curve. The construction is based on a specific choice of the angular function that governs the curve's tangent indicatrix, leading to integrable expressions.

entry.title: A Differentiable, GPU-Accelerated Finite-Element Formulation in JAX for Large-Deformation Shells with Contact: Application to Patient-Specific Aortic Valve Simulation
entry.summary: Patient-specific aortic-valve models can help assess how tissue properties and geometry influence leaflet deformation and coaptation, with potential to inform intervention planning. Large deformations, near-incompressibility, and evolving contact make these simulations computationally demanding and can challenge nonlinear convergence. Differentiable, GPU-accelerated methods offer efficient derivative evaluation and parallel computation, but their matrix-free application to soft-tissue shells with contact remains less established. We developed a forward solver using tatva's energy-based finite-element framework in JAX. The solver combines finite-strain extensible-director shells, hyperelastic constitutive models, and a finite-range repulsive contact energy. Nonlinear equilibrium is solved using a regularized, matrix-free Newton-Krylov method with two-level preconditioning. Automatic differentiation evaluates tangent-vector products without forming or storing the primary tangent matrix, while GPU execution parallelizes element and quadrature-point computations. Constitutive, shell, contact, and self-contact responses were assessed against analytical, semi-analytical, and published benchmarks. At a contact-free plate equilibrium, implicit sensitivities of the converged apex displacement to constitutive parameters, thickness, and pressure agreed with finite differences from independent nonlinear simulations. Simulations of three patient-specific aortic-valve models (two tricuspid and one bicuspid) achieved final relative equilibrium residuals below 10^-4. Median GPU runtimes were approximately 15-25 minutes, with 5.3-6.5-fold speedups relative to corresponding CPU runs on the tested hardware. These results provide component-level verification and demonstrate GPU-accelerated forward valve simulation in the tested cases, supporting future gradient-based inverse studies.

entry.title: Episodic Plasma Flows and Coronal Brightenings in an Arch Filament System Observed with SUNRISE III
entry.summary: Emerging flux regions (EFRs) transport magnetic flux and release energy in the solar atmosphere, often hosting arch filament systems (AFSs). We present high-resolution observations of an EFR obtained with Sunrise III, combining the Tunable Magnetograph (TuMag), the Sunrise Chromospheric Infrared Spectro-Polarimeter (SCIP), and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). The dataset follows an AFS continuously for nearly four hours. Line-of-sight (LOS) velocities derived from the Mg I b$_2$ line reveal three episodic plasma-flow events, with downflows reaching approximately 17 km s$^{-1}$ at the footpoints and enhanced upflows near the loop tops. Although this pattern agrees with the classical emergence and draining scenario, the strongest upflows and downflows occur nearly simultaneously. Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) observations at 304 and 171 Angstrom reveal transient extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) brightenings in the surrounding emerging system. Some occur during enhanced-flow episodes, while others do not, indicating that the temporal correspondence is not systematic. Multiline spectropolarimetric inversions reveal temperatures between approximately 4000 and 10,000 K and a smooth variation of magnetic field inclination along a representative AFS loop. Non-force-free-field extrapolations provide the large-scale magnetic context of the low-lying AFS loops and surrounding coronal structures. Together, the observations reveal a spatially and temporally complex evolution without establishing a direct causal connection between local plasma-flow enhancements and EUV brightenings.

entry.title: Using Gauge Covariant Lie Derivatives in Poincaré Gauge and Metric Teleparallel Theories of Gravity
entry.summary: A procedure to determine the initial ansatz for the co-frame and spin connection characterizing a Riemann-Cartan geometry respecting a given group of continuous symmetries is illustrated. Assuming invariance of the metric under a particular group of symmetries, this gauge covariant Lie derivative when applied to the metric and associated orthonormal co-frame determines the values of an antisymmetric compensating matrix. The gauge covariant Lie derivative of the spin connection depends on this matrix, which when solved yields the spin connection compatible with the chosen co-frame. The procedure is straightforward and can be employed for any Riemann-Cartan geometry having symmetries including those with a non-trivial isotropy subgroup. Here we illustrate the procedure with numerous examples, including, spherically symmetric, plane symmetric, locally rotationally symmetric Bianchi type III, Gödel, de Sitter and anti-de Sitter geometries. Further, we have also solved the zero curvature constraint to obtain the resulting spin connection for the corresponding metric teleparallel geometry having this same symmetry group. We complete this investigation by including the Lorentz transformation that yields the proper frame for some of these metric teleparallel geometries. This investigation provides a kinematical framework useful for the further study of Poincaré Gauge and metric teleparallel theories of gravity.

entry.title: On the source algebra equivalence class of blocks with cyclic defect groups, II
entry.summary: This series of papers is a contribution to the program of classifying $p$-blocks of finite groups up to source algebra equivalence, starting with the case of cyclic blocks. To any $p$-block $\mathbf{B}$ of a finite group with cyclic defect group $D$, Linckelmann associated an invariant $W( \mathbf{B} )$, which is an indecomposable endo-permutation module over $D$, and which, together with the Brauer tree of $\mathbf{B}$, essentially determines its source algebra equivalence class. In Parts II-IV of our series of papers, we classify, for odd $p$, those endo-permutation modules of cyclic $p$-groups arising from $p$-blocks of quasisimple groups. In the present Part II, we reduce the desired classification for the quasisimple classical groups of Lie type $B$, $C$, and $D$ to the corresponding objective for the general linear and unitary groups; the classification is completed for the latter groups.

entry.title: Monotonicity, continuity and differentiability results for the $L^p$ Hardy constant
entry.summary: We consider the $L^p$ Hardy inequality involving the distance to the boundary for a domain in the $n$-dimensional Euclidean space. We study the dependence on $p$ of the corresponding best constant and we prove monotonicity, continuity and differentiability results. The focus is on non-convex domains in which case such constant is in general not explicitly known.

entry.title: Topological interfaces between universes and generalized families of 2d QFTs
entry.summary: Two-dimensional quantum field theories with topological point operators decompose into universes. Just as fusion categories have played an important role in understanding non-invertible symmetries, multi-fusion categories play an analogous role for the symmetries of such decomposing theories. We describe a finite symmetry as a multi-fusion category together with its action functor, which keeps track of trivially acting symmetries and of the topological interfaces between universes. Relative to a chosen symmetry, we classify pairs of universes by the topological interfaces it contains, which reflect the structure of the multi-fusion category: universes in different indecomposable summands are joined by no interface (Type~III), while within a summand they are related by invertible (Type~I) or only non-invertible (Type~II) interfaces. For orbifolds with a trivially acting abelian normal subgroup, we derive the full inherited symmetry, which characterizes the operators between universes found case by case by Robbins, Sharpe and Vandermeulen and yields pairs of Types~I and~II but never of Type~III. We construct Type~III pairs instead from extensions of $2$-group type and from renormalization group flows out of a common ultraviolet theory. Finally, we propose a correspondence with the generalized families of quantum field theories of Brennan and Intriligator, in which equivariant families correspond to Type~I pairs and categorical ones to Type~II pairs whose gauging preserves the symmetry, family anomalies appear as universes carrying different symmetry-protected topological phases, and Type~III pairs can realize families over a discrete parameter. An appendix by Xingyang Yu works out the higher-charge Schwinger model as a Lagrangian example.

entry.title: Reverse Module Categories of Vertex Operator Algebras
entry.summary: We study the realization of the reverse braided category of the module category of a rational vertex operator algebra V. Using holomorphic extensions and commutant constructions, we prove that this realization property is preserved under suitable cosets, tensor products, extensions, and finite-group orbifolds. As applications, we establish the property for unitary Virasoro minimal models, affine vertex operator algebras of types ABCDE at positive integral levels, the corresponding principal W-algebras of type ADE, and related parafermion vertex operator algebras.
