entry.title: Sample Complexity for Generative Learning of Quantum Measurement Data
entry.summary: Generative learning of a quantum measurement distribution from finite data requires choosing a model capacity that balances representation accuracy against estimation cost. We develop a bias-variance framework that decomposes the expected population Kullback-Leibler error at model capacity $s$ and sample size $N$ as $E(s,N)=B(s)+V(s,N)$, with representation bias $B$ and a variance term $V$ capturing the mean estimation error. In the well-sampled regime, $V(s,N)\simeq[NC(s)]^{-1}$, and exponential or algebraic laws for $B$ and $C$ yield four scaling templates for the optimal error, from inverse powers of $N$ to inverse powers of $\ln N$. For local autoregressive models, the context radius sets the model capacity, and $B$ is the summed conditional mutual information lost by truncating the context. For a smoothed histogram learner, we derive an exact finite-sample estimation cost that accounts for rarely observed contexts and recovers the parameter-count law in the well-sampled regime. For transverse-field Ising Born distributions, the independently evaluated bias and estimation cost predict both the optimal context radius and the optimal error. In the well-sampled regime, the estimation cost grows exponentially with context radius. Its competition with approximately exponential bias decay in the gapped regimes predicts power-law error decay in $N$, while algebraic bias decay at criticality predicts asymptotic inverse-power decay in $\ln N$. Bulk-site results are consistent with the corresponding finite-sample predictions. These results connect the structure of quantum measurement distributions to the model capacity justified by finite data.

entry.title: WovenAnchor Matcher: Specialized Intra- and Inter-Image Context Modeling for Feature Matching
entry.summary: Semi-dense local feature matching commonly aggregates contextual information before coarse-to-fine correspondence estimation. However, intra-image and inter-image aggregation serve different roles: the former should propagate spatial evidence within each image while retaining structured two-dimensional dependencies, whereas the latter should gather information from plausible corresponding regions while limiting noise from unrelated locations. We propose WovenAnchor Matcher (WAM), a semi-dense matching framework based on role-specialized context aggregation. WAM introduces two complementary operators. WovenMamba performs intra-image aggregation through horizontal-then-vertical state-space propagation, allowing vertical updates to operate on horizontally contextualized features and thereby encouraging a structured two-dimensional receptive-field bias. AnchorCrossAttention performs inter-image aggregation by using cross-attention to gather context from plausible corresponding regions across the image pair. It performs this exchange over local representative anchors that aggregate feature evidence within each window. On MegaDepth, WAM achieves 66.1 pose AUC@5$^\circ$, improving on the JamMa baseline by 2.0 AUC points under the same evaluation setup. Ablations show that removing or replacing either specialized component reduces accuracy, providing evidence that intra-image propagation and inter-image retrieval benefit from role-specific aggregation designs. Code and pretrained weights are available at https://github.com/mmaiLab/WovenAnchorMatcher.

entry.title: A General Topological Symmetry Index for Critical Orbits In Neural Network Loss Landscapes
entry.summary: A systematic understanding of the global structure of neural-network loss landscapes remains challenging due to their high dimensionality. Symmetries arising from network architectures and learning objectives provide a way to investigate aspects of this structure. Although a growing number of studies have drawn attention to these symmetries, a systematic characterization of them, as well as of the critical orbits they give rise to, remains incomplete. To address this gap, in this work we establish a topological symmetry index, based on the methodologies from the family of equivariant degree theories, to decode these symmetries. The frameworks apply to arbitrary network architectures and include methods applicable to degenerate critical orbits. The index detects the isotropy of the critical points and quantifies the corresponding net topological contributions. Several examples, including softplus MLPs, Transformers, and equivariant neural networks, are presented to illustrate the computations.

entry.title: Recovery of Rough Sources in the Inverse Monge-Ampère Problem
entry.summary: We prove that every nonnegative $L^1$ source in the Monge-Ampère equation \[ \det D^2u=f\quad\text{in }Ω, \] on a bounded uniformly convex $C^{1,1}$ domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$, is uniquely determined by generalized boundary measurements of Alexandrov solutions. The measurement is the extremal boundary slope, which extends the classical outward normal derivative and may take the value $+\infty$. For each direction $ω\in\mathbb S^{n-1}$, it suffices to know these slopes for cylindrical Dirichlet data $\frac{t_k^ω}{2}|P_ωx|^2$ along any sequence $t_k^ω\to\infty$, where $P_ω$ projects onto $ω^\perp$. The boundary value and extremal slope determine the interior subgradient image up to a Lebesgue null set. An exact change of variables formula then converts equality of these images into integral identities for the source, and a large-amplitude limit recovers its Euclidean X-ray transform. This yields uniqueness without a positive lower bound on the source. For nonnegative $L^\infty$ sources, the extremal slopes are bounded and agree with the interior normal derivatives, giving a Dirichlet-to-interior-Neumann formulation. We also extend the inverse argument to the gradient-weighted equation \[ \vartheta(\nabla u)\det D^2u=f, \] where the known weight $\vartheta$ is locally integrable, Borel measurable, and bounded below by a positive constant. We prove existence of the corresponding Alexandrov solutions and show that the same cylindrical boundary-slope data uniquely determine every nonnegative $L^1$ source.

entry.title: Disentangling Latent Embeddings with Sparse Linear Concept Cones (SLiCC)
entry.summary: Pretrained vision models encode semantic information in latent embedding spaces that are useful for downstream tasks. We hypothesize that this information can be disentangled to separate the content of complex scenes by decomposing each embedding into multiple concept-specific components. We propose Sparse Linear Concept Cones (SLiCC), a supervised dictionary learning approach that estimates a linear synthesis model consisting of sparse, non-negative combinations of groups of dictionary atoms, whose group-wise activity is guided by multi-label information. Each concept-specific component is a non-negative combination of atoms associated with a label and lies in a corresponding concept cone. We introduce an alternating optimization algorithm and an autoencoder formulation of SLiCC. We apply SLiCC to three types of CLIP and DINOv2 embeddings across five datasets. For CLIP, we additionally exploit image-text alignment to enable a self-supervised SLiCC. We also introduce a fully unsupervised autoencoder that enforces group sparsity based on the norm of neuron activations. Quantitative results show that supervised SLiCC improves concept-filtered image retrieval over unfiltered embeddings, including retrieval of finer-grained information not provided during training. Beyond retrieval of individual concepts, the disentangled components enable concept deletion and recombination across images. We further explore conditional image generation using Image-to-Prompt, with qualitative results illustrating retrieval and generation from manipulated concept representations.

entry.title: On the Spherical Dirichlet Distribution: Corrections and Results
entry.summary: This article revisits the spherical-Dirichlet distribution (SDD) introduced by Guardiola (2020) and clarifies the correction to its density presented in an earlier version of this preprint. The principal issue concerns Equation (3) of the original publication, which expresses the density in local Euclidean coordinates rather than with respect to spherical surface-area measure. We derive the corrected intrinsic density and revisit its moments, covariance matrix, mode, and limiting properties. We show that the two density representations describe the same probability distribution, preserving the moment formulas and likelihood-based parameter estimation. However, the mode and uniformity conditions depend on the reference measure and require corresponding clarification. Reported simulation and text mining estimates are revisited and updated. The resulting presentation reconciles the original construction with its intrinsic spherical properties.

entry.title: From Entanglement Bootstrap to DHR Theory
entry.summary: We establish a direct connection between the entanglement bootstrap and the Doplicher--Haag--Roberts theory of superselection sectors for two-dimensional quantum spin systems. Under the entanglement-bootstrap assumptions, we prove Haag duality and establish a one-to-one correspondence between simple entanglement-bootstrap anyon types and irreducible superselection sectors. For each fusion channel, we further construct an affine bijection from density matrices on the entanglement-bootstrap fusion space to normalized positive intertwiners in the corresponding operator-algebraic fusion channel. These results connect the entropic and operator-algebraic descriptions of anyons directly, without passing through exactly solvable lattice models.

entry.title: SelectSep: Target-Selective Video Queries for Audio Source Separation
entry.summary: Video-queried sound separation (VQSS) aims to isolate a target sound from an audio mixture using its corresponding video as a query. However, scene-level video queries can become ambiguous when multiple sounding objects are visible, particularly when the target and interferer are semantically similar. We propose SelectSep, a target-selective VQSS framework that jointly uses text and a single click coordinate to specify the target source and instance without requiring segmentation at inference time. We adapt the visual encoder through target-feature distillation with text and click conditioning, and then fine-tune the separator using the adapted visual features. We also introduce an on-screen interference setting, where both the target and interferer are visible, to evaluate target selectivity. Experiments on standard benchmarks and the on-screen interference setting demonstrate consistent improvements in separation quality and target selectivity, particularly for mixtures containing semantically similar sources.

entry.title: Bound-preserving and mass-conserving projection BCFD methods for incompressible miscible displacement in porous media
entry.summary: In this paper, we propose and analyze two novel structure-preserving projection schemes for the incompressible miscible displacement problem in porous media. These schemes are specifically designed to preserve two essential physical properties--concentration bounds and the mass balance identity, and are accompanied by a rigorous error analysis for the projection approach. Both schemes are second-order accurate in space but differ in temporal accuracy: one is first-order and the other is second-order. Methodologically, both schemes comprise a prediction step for the concentration variable, based on a second-order modified upwind discretization together with an implicit-explicit finite difference approximation, followed by a projection (or correction) step that enforces the desired physical constraints, namely bounds and mass conservation. For the first-order temporal scheme, the velocity and pressure are solved at the first step on staggered spatial grids with explicit treatment of concentration. In contrast, for the second-order scheme, to ensure well-posedness and to suppress non-physical oscillations in the simulation, the velocity and pressure are solved at the final step with the concentration treated implicitly. A rigorous numerical theoretical framework is established for the first-order scheme, encompassing optimal-order error estimates, stability, and proofs of the existence and uniqueness of the numerical solutions. The numerical analysis framework is further extended to the more involved second-order scheme, and the corresponding theoretical results are briefly outlined. Finally, numerical examples, including some 'real' simulations, are presented to verify the theoretical findings and demonstrate the strong performance of the proposed schemes. In particular, the occurrence of viscous fingering is successfully captured and confirmed by the numerical results.

entry.title: Two-Layer Microwave Linear Analog Computer (MiLAC)-Aided Multi-User MIMO Networks
entry.summary: Microwave linear analog computer (MiLAC)-aided beamforming, which performs signal processing directly in the analog domain, has recently emerged as a promising alternative to fully digital and hybrid beamforming for multi-antenna systems. However, existing studies have shown that a single lossless and reciprocal MiLAC at the transmitter cannot, in general, attain the performance of fully digital beamforming in multi-user scenarios. To overcome this limitation, we propose a two-layer MiLAC-aided transmit beamforming architecture for downlink multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) networks. Leveraging multiport microwave network theory, we first establish a general physics-compliant model of the proposed architecture, and then derive a simplified model under the assumptions of unilateral and perfectly matched amplifiers. We prove that, with lossless and reciprocal MiLACs, the two-layer MiLAC-aided transmitter can realize any fully digital transmit beamformer, while a single-layer MiLAC-aided receiver can attain the same achievable rate as a fully digital linear combiner. We then derive closed-form mappings from fully digital transmit beamformers and receive combiners to their corresponding MiLAC-aided analog implementations. Based on these equivalence results, we formulate a sum-rate maximization problem for the considered multi-user MIMO network and develop an optimization framework for jointly designing the power allocation and scattering matrices of the MiLAC-aided transceivers. Numerical results validate the theoretical analysis and show that the proposed two-layer MiLAC-aided design attains the same sum-rate performance as its fully digital counterpart.

entry.title: Exponential decay of threshold correlations for symmetric periodic functions
entry.summary: We study how often $n$ distinct integer dilates of a periodic function can all lie above a fixed threshold or all lie below its negative. We consider continuous functions $f:\mathbb R\to[-1,1]$ that are $1$-periodic, even, strictly decreasing on $[0,1/2]$, and satisfy $f(0)=1$ and $f(t+1/2)=-f(t)$. This class includes the cosine and the triangle wave. For $0\leqα<1$, let $ρ_α\in(0,1/4]$ be determined by $f(ρ_α)=α$, and let $F_α(n)$ denote the infimum of these proportions over all sets of $n$ distinct positive integer frequencies. We prove that $F_α(n)\geq 4ρ_α^n$ and that the limit $\lim_{n\to\infty}F_α(n)^{1/n}$ exists for every threshold. When $ρ_α^{-1}$ is an integer, we obtain \begin{align} F_α(n) &\leq C_αn^{\log_2((1-ρ_α)/(1-2ρ_α))}ρ_α^n, \end{align} and hence the limit equals $ρ_α$. Otherwise, the limit belongs to the interval $[ρ_α,\lfloorρ_α^{-1}\rfloor^{-1}]$. The upper bound in the reciprocal case uses a cyclic covering construction previously studied in the context of circular graphs. We give a self-contained proof of the corresponding optimal modulus.

entry.title: $L^\infty$ blow-up in the fourth-order Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation
entry.summary: We investigate the fourth-order Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation $$ u_{tttt}+αu_{ttt}+βu_{tt}-γΔu_{tt}-δΔu_{t}-\varrho Δu=(f(u))_{ttt}+(f(u))_{tt} $$ under homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions in a smooth bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\leq 3$, where $α\in \mathbb{R}$ and $β,γ,δ,\varrho>0$. First, for any suitably regular initial data and assuming that $f\in C^4(\mathbb{R})$ with $f(0)=0$, we prove that the corresponding initial-boundary value problem admits a unique maximal strong solution $u$ on $(0, T_{max})$. Second, by combining three time-integrated formulations with a series of resolvent-regularized energy estimates, we show that gradient blow-up is ruled out in the sense that \begin{equation} \tag{*} T_{max}<\infty \quad\,\, \Rightarrow\quad\,\, \limsup_{t\nearrow T_{max}}\|u(\cdot,t)\|_{L^{\infty}(Ω)}=\infty. \end{equation} Finally, assuming in addition that $f$ is convex and grows superlinearly in the sense that $$ f''(ξ)\geq 0 \;\; \mbox{ for all}\;\;ξ\in\mathbb{R}, \qquad \frac{f(ξ)}ξ\rightarrow +\infty\;\;\mbox{ as}\;\; ξ\rightarrow +\infty , \qquad \int_{ξ_{0}}^{\infty}\frac{dξ}{f(ξ)}<\infty \;\; \mbox{ for some}\;\; ξ_{0}>0, $$ we employ the extensibility criterion (*) to prove that, for a suitable class of initial data, the solution blows up in finite time in the $L^\infty$-norm. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first rigorous description of finite-time blow-up for a genuinely nonlinear equation of fourth order in time.

entry.title: Series approximation of discrete-soliton solutions of the DNLS equation
entry.summary: We study standing waves of the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger (DNLS) equation by means of perturbative series expansions in the inter-site coupling parameter $\varepsilon$. Power-series approximations are derived for three representative configurations: a single-site soliton and the two two-site ones, namely the in-phase and the out-of-phase configurations. Although higher-order truncations are increasingly accurate for small $\varepsilon$, the expansions possess a small radius of convergence and cease to be useful well before $\varepsilon={\cal O}(1)$. To extend their range of validity we apply the Euler convergence-acceleration method, constructing an optimally transformed series for each lattice site individually. The transformed solution is shown to have substantially better convergence radius and preserves the localization of the solution much better than the original series solution. We then insert the series profiles into the linearization matrix of the DNLS equation in order to obtain improved approximations of the stability eigenvalues, with particular attention to the unstable real eigenvalue of the in-phase configuration. Optimal truncation of the corresponding expansion yields a closed-form ${\cal O}(\varepsilon^{5/2})$ estimate, which significantly extends the known ${\cal O}(\varepsilon^{1/2})$ leading-order result to considerably larger couplings, while the semi-numerical use of the accelerated profiles reproduces the numerically computed eigenvalue to values of $\varepsilon$ of ${\cal O}(1)$. Throughout, both the solution profiles and their stability eigenvalues are benchmarked against the numerical solution obtained through a continuation procedure from the anti-continuum limit.

entry.title: IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation
entry.summary: Humans routinely consume multimodal content, where textual and visual information is naturally interleaved. Although Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) can jointly generate text and images, multimodal interleaved generation remains largely underexplored. Progress in this area is hindered by two key limitations: (1) the lack of well-defined interleaved generation tasks and corresponding training data, and (2) the absence of fine-grained evaluation protocols that can reliably diagnose model performance across different capability dimensions. To this end, we present IntReal, comprising two complementary components: IntReal-100K, a real-world dataset of multimodal interleaved samples spanning four major categories, and the IntReal Evaluation Suite, which evaluates model performance across seven complementary dimensions using specialized expert models, enabling coarse-to-fine diagnosis. Extensive experiments validate our evaluation suite through low inter-metric redundancy (max pairwise absolute Spearman's $ρ\leq 0.42$ ), high agreement with human judgments (83.3% accuracy), and strong consistency across different expert evaluators (Spearman's $ρ> 0.9$ ), supporting the complementarity and reliability of our metrics. By benchmarking four families of UMMs, we show that IntReal Evaluation Suite reveals distinct strengths and weaknesses across models. Post-training experiments demonstrate the utility of IntReal-100K for improving interleaved generation and further show that training unimodal generation can also benefit interleaved generation. These findings suggest that interleaved generation can benefit from modality-specific optimization, rather than requiring joint text-image training at every stage.

entry.title: Logarithmic fractional Hardy inequalities
entry.summary: We establish sharp fractional Hardy inequalities in the critical regimes $sp=d$ and $sp=1$, with explicit logarithmic weight functions. In the whole-space setting, for $p>d\ge 1$, $sp=d$, we prove that \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^d} \int_{\mathbb R^d} \frac{|u(x)-u(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{2d}}\,dx\,dy \geq \left(\frac{p-1}{p}\right)^p \int_{B_R}|u(x)|^p W_{p,d,R}(x)\,dx, \end{equation*} for $u\in C_c(B_R)$, where $W_{p,d,R}$ is a logarithmic-type weight and the constant is sharp. We also show that the corresponding inequality with the simpler weight $|x|^{-d}(\log(R/|x|))^{-p}$ cannot hold with any positive constant. Furthermore, we derive two-sided estimates and asymptotic formulae for $W_{p,d,R}$, including its limiting connection with the classical Hardy inequality. In the half-space $\mathbb{R}^{d}_{+}$, we establish an analogous sharp fractional Hardy inequality in the critical case $sp=1$, with an explicit logarithmic weight depending on the distance to the boundary. We also investigate the asymptotic behaviour of this weight, obtaining estimates that describe its behaviour near the boundary. These results elucidate the role of logarithmic weights in critical fractional Hardy inequalities in both whole-space and half-space settings.

entry.title: BiliPicks: Seven Years of Weekly Platform Curation on Bilibili with Video Metadata, Comments, and Danmaku
entry.summary: BiliPicks documents seven years of Bilibili's Weekly Picks, a platform-curated editorial video series. The dataset covers 371 publicly listed issues and 13,758 curated videos from 22 March 2019 to 7 May 2026. It links issue dates, themes and editorial recommendations to video metadata, 47,799,657 top-level comments, 125,690,760 time-synchronised overlay comments (danmaku), and 13,739 cover images. Weekly issues provide a consistent unit for tracing changes in category composition, recurring creators and editorial framing. Corresponding comments and danmaku connect video-level discussion with audience expressions tied to particular moments, while covers add a visual dimension. We evaluate retrieval coverage and illustrate longitudinal analyses of selection, audience language and cover presentation. BiliPicks provides a dataset for future studies of platform curation, linking changes in published selections to their editorial framing and corresponding audience engagement.

entry.title: The Reality Gap in Automated Driving Systems Testing: Landscape, Challenges, and Research Directions
entry.summary: Simulation is essential for testing automated driving systems (ADS), but discrepancies between simulation and reality can undermine testing conclusions. It remains unclear which discrepancies the literature addresses and what evidence supports correspondence claims. We present a systematic mapping of 235 primary studies that measure or mitigate the reality gap in ADS testing, selected from 4,195 publications. We characterise objectives, targets, approaches, experimental setups, and evaluation evidence. Our classification distinguishes simulated and real-world execution across six ADS test components, separately for each approach and its evaluation reference. This distinguishes real-world information used to construct an approach from evidence used to evaluate its claims. Of the included studies, 76% address mitigation, primarily targeting scenario and actor realism and perception, while 94% report validation or measurement procedures. Only 61 studies report metrics from multiple families covering sensor/perception correspondence, ADS behaviour, vehicle dynamics, or safety outcomes; this coverage does not establish causal links between discrepancies and test verdicts. The synthesis highlights that real-world content and physical execution must be interpreted against the claim evaluated. The findings motivate claim-specific evaluation and component-level reporting to establish which discrepancies affect testing conclusions and when simulation evidence supports conclusions about real-world ADS behaviour.

entry.title: Teleparallel Renormalization of Gravitational Action
entry.summary: We study the gravitational action in the teleparallel equivalent of general relativity, where the spin connection contributes to the action through a surface term and, when chosen appropriately, regularizes the action by effectively playing the role of a counterterm. We resolve several apparent ambiguities in this procedure using the Schwarzschild spacetime as an example. We show that the apparent discrepancy between bulk and quasilocal actions originates from contributions associated with spacetime singularities, and that the quasilocal action agrees with the standard results obtained in general relativity. We further clarify the role of the tetrad choice in determining the corresponding spin connection, showing that the proper diagonal and canonical frames give the same Euclidean action, while only the proper diagonal frame reproduces the expected Lorentzian action on the Wheeler--DeWitt patch. Finally, we establish the uniqueness of the regularization scheme and show that imposing an appropriate fall-off behavior of the torsion tensor removes the remaining ambiguity and fixes the Euclidean action uniquely.

entry.title: Giant piezomagnetic response driven by spin reorientation in the topological Kagome magnet TbMn6Sn6
entry.summary: Achieving a large strain response to a small magnetic-field variation remains a challenge in magnetomechanical materials, particularly in topological systems where the coupling between spin reconstruction and lattice deformation remains unclear. Here, we report an anomalous magnetostrictive response associated with field-induced spin reorientation in the topological Kagome magnet TbMn6Sn6. Below its spin-reorientation temperature of 310 K, an in-plane magnetic field induces an abrupt increase in magnetostriction, which exceeds 120 ppm at 240 K. This transition produces a giant differential piezomagnetic coefficient of approximately 5000 ppm T-1, far exceeding the values reported for other topological magnetic materials and commercial FeGa alloys, and placing TbMn6Sn6 among the most field-sensitive magnetostrictive materials. The field position of this peak agrees with the anomalies in magnetization and magnetotransport, demonstrating that the large differential response is tied to field-induced spin reorientation. Thermal expansion also changes across the spin-reorientation boundary. Raman measurements reveal corresponding anomalies in phonon energy and linewidth, indicating that the reorientation modifies the lattice dynamics. The combined results support a mechanism in which competing magnetic anisotropies of the Tb and Mn sublattices, coupled through Tb-Mn exchange, create magnetic configurations with different equilibrium strains. This finding establishes spin reorientation as a route to giant piezomagnetic responses in topological magnets and provides a basis for magnetomechanical sensing and switching near room temperature.

entry.title: Structure-retained low-rank adapters for weather synthesis
entry.summary: Real-world deployment of computer vision models, particularly in outdoor scenarios, is often limited by environmental interferences, such as adverse weather. Improving model robustness across weather conditions is thus critical for reliability. However, sourcing high-quality data relevant to isolated weather effects is a significant challenge. Most datasets include changes in dynamic elements across observations of the same scene: subjects such as pedestrians and vehicles change between shots, while camera viewpoints vary. These aspects make it difficult to decouple solely weather-induced distribution shifts from the scene. In this work, we address this with a novel weather synthesis framework that utilizes structure-retaining Low-Rank Adapters (LoRA). We analyze the attention blocks in Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL) and identify where relevant structural information is mostly processed during image-to-image translation. Through an architectural analysis of SDXL, we learn structural LoRA matrices for the corresponding blocks and then leverage them for weather synthesis, eliminating the need for external conditioning such as ControlNet. Experimental results demonstrate that our method improves upon existing synthesis approaches, achieving greater realism while preserving structure. This provides a robust pipeline for generating high-fidelity training and evaluation data for outdoor computer vision applications.

entry.title: ETA-Motion: Efficient Topology-Agnostic Motion Diffusion via Sparse Joint Learning
entry.summary: Topology-agnostic motion generation aims to synthesize motions for diverse characters with arbitrary skeletons. Unlike conventional motion generation, which assumes a fixed skeletal template, this setting must handle diverse joint configurations and inconsistent joint semantics across characters. Existing methods address this challenge through dense full-joint modeling, which incurs substantial computational cost and hinders learning transferable motion patterns across diverse skeletal topologies. We present ETA-Motion, a topology-agnostic motion generation framework based on sparse joint learning. Instead of learning motion from all joints, our method uses a compact subset of joints to reduce redundancy and trains the motion generator on the resulting sparse skeleton. To facilitate correspondence across diverse topologies, we introduce semantic joint embeddings that combine textual and visual cues, together with topology-aware training objectives for preserving skeletal structure. Although ETA-Motion is trained only on sparse skeletal observations, it supports full-skeleton motion generation during inference. Experimental results demonstrate that ETA-Motion outperforms existing topology-agnostic baselines while significantly improving efficiency and generalization to unseen motions and unseen topologies.

entry.title: Scalable Bayesian Quadrature via Operator-Adapted Features
entry.summary: Kernel methods face two recurrent bottlenecks: the cubic cost of inverting an $n\times n$ kernel matrix, as in kernel ridge regression, and the evaluation of kernel integrals, as required in kernel quadrature. Existing low-rank kernel and Gaussian process approximations primarily address the former bottleneck, but do not control the downstream quadrature error when both the kernel matrix and kernel mean are approximated, particularly when the integrand lies outside the kernel reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We address both challenges through an operator-adapted finite-feature approximation. Specifically, we construct a finite-dimensional working kernel from the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a second-order differential operator. We establish convergence guarantees for the resulting finite-feature estimators in kernel quadrature, with extension to other related kernel methods. Our results show that, with $m \lesssim n$ basis functions, the truncated estimator attains the corresponding benchmark statistical rates. The theory covers fixed/random designs, noisy/noiseless observations, oversmoothing/undersmoothing regimes, and Matérn/Gaussian-type weights. We provide explicit error bounds that quantify the roles of the spectral cutoff, regularization parameter, lengthscale, sampling geometry, and operator boundary condition. We verify the convergence results in numerical experiments.

entry.title: Graph-diameter criteria and sharp dissipation in discrete Wasserstein-Fisher geometry
entry.summary: We study the probability simplex of a finite connected weighted graph with an Onsager operator combining logarithmic-mean transport and mass-conserving Fisher reaction. For every fixed positive reaction parameter, we prove that the entropy Hessian has a finite global lower bound if and only if the original transport graph has diameter at most two. Near a boundary probability, the corresponding criterion is that its positive support reaches every vertex in at most two steps. The proof controls all potential directions under arbitrary multiscale boundary degeneration. For graphs of diameter at most two, the optimal lower bound is Lipschitz on bounded parameter intervals, including the pure-transport endpoint. We also determine the largest instantaneous logarithmic-amplitude dissipation function depending only on the graph and the current amplitude, and construct two-level probabilities attaining it. Its positivity has the same two-step criterion. As consequences, we obtain graph-dependent entropy-decay estimates and exact projective contraction bounds without assuming nonnegative entropic curvature.

entry.title: A Kohnen-Zagier Formula in Level 1
entry.summary: In 1985 Kohnen used the Shimura correspondence to prove a general formula relating the coefficients of half-integral weight modular forms of level $ 4N $ transforming with respect to the theta multiplier to central values of $ L $-functions for twists of newforms of level $ N $. This generalized previous work with Zagier. In this paper, we prove a Kohnen-Zagier type formula using Yang's Shimura correspondence for powers of the eta multiplier in level $ 1 $, relating the coefficients of half-integral weight modular forms to central values of $ L $-functions for twists of newforms of level $ 6 $. To do so we develop some of the theory of modular forms transforming with respect to powers of the eta multiplier and introduce Shintani lifts of level $ 6 $, with Fourier coefficients given in terms of cycle integrals.

entry.title: Number of ends of conjugacy diagrams
entry.summary: For each $n\geq 2$, we construct a finitely generated group $W_n$ with a conjugacy class such that the conjugacy diagram of this class has exactly $n$ ends. For this class, we compute the quotient spaces of the space of derivations of the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[W_n]$ modulo quasi-inner and inner derivations, as well as the corresponding component of the first Hochschild cohomology.

entry.title: Integrating multi-source local information for global undirected graph reconstruction via integer programming
entry.summary: Graphical models are widely used to represent conditional independence structures, but learning them is challenging when data are fragmented across sources that measure different subsets of variables and may not be directly shareable. We develop a general framework for reconstructing a shared global graph from heterogeneous, partially observed sources. Our framework permits both the observed variable sets and source-specific distributions to differ. Under a source-wise faithfulness condition, local conditional independence graphs correspond to latent projections of the shared global graph, which is identifiable up to the equivalence class induced by the observed variable sets. The framework integrates raw data, estimated source graphs, or a combination of both, accommodating settings with restricted access to individual-level data, such as privacy constraints. We develop mixed-integer optimization formulations and scalable approximate algorithms for several classes of graphical models. Unlike standard high-dimensional analyses, our guarantees are governed by new combinatorial notions of signal strength that capture how information propagates across partially observed sources. Extensive simulations further show that integration can substantially improve estimation of source-specific projected graphs relative to separate source methods. Real-data application illustrates the framework's use with partially-observed sources of fatty acid measurements.

entry.title: Beyond fabrication: Misattributed numbers in papers written by AI research agents
entry.summary: Verifying numerical claims in research written by AI agents is an important but challenging problem. Recent benchmarks show that many agent-written papers fail integrity checks, but such verdicts, often produced by a single LLM judge, identify failure without explaining its nature, and existing checks either test a paper for internal consistency or test whether a reported value appears somewhere in an agent's output. We re-analyze all 540 released judgments from a recent public benchmark of AI research agents (nine agents, fifteen open research problems) and manually label 256 numerical claims from 18 submissions. Failures concentrate on alignment between the paper and the underlying work rather than overt cheating, and about four in five unsupported claims correspond to values in the agent's own files that come from the wrong experiment, metric, or run. We introduce a deterministic claim-to-evidence checker that scores whether the surrounding context identifies the claimed result and calibrates each claim against numerical decoys. With its rules fixed before labeling, it certifies claims with over 90% precision against blinded annotators (78 of 85; Cohen's kappa = 0.89), while verifying only a subset of claims; most claims it cannot verify are nevertheless traceable, so failure to verify is not evidence of falsehood. An LLM verifier given the same evidence recovers more traceable claims but accepts about three times as many misattributed ones, so the two are best used together. Applied to 99 submissions, the checker reveals large differences in traceability across agents, and a second judge from a different vendor preserves the official agent ranking while passing twice as many papers. These findings motivate provenance-first auditing of AI-produced research.

entry.title: Sublinear Algorithms for Estimating Single-Linkage Clustering Costs
entry.summary: Single-linkage clustering (SLC) is a fundamental method for hierarchical data analysis. In the distance setting, a $k$-clustering produced by SLC can be obtained by computing a minimum spanning tree (MST) and deleting its $k-1$ heaviest edges. This naturally induces a cost profile for the SLC hierarchy: for each $k\in[n]$, we define $\mathrm{cost}_k$ to be the weight of the resulting $k$-component spanning forest, equivalently, the minimum total weight of any spanning forest with exactly $k$ connected components. The corresponding \emph{SLC cost profile} is $(\mathrm{cost}_1,\ldots,\mathrm{cost}_n)$, and the scalar quantity $\mathrm{cost}(G)=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\mathrm{cost}_k$ is the area under this profile. We study the problem of approximating these quantities in sublinear time. We assume that the input is a weighted graph $G$ of average degree $d$ with edge weights in $\{1,\dots,W\}$, accessed through adjacency-list queries; missing edges are treated as having infinite distance. Our main result is a sampling-based algorithm that outputs a succinct sketch of the entire SLC cost profile in the distance setting. The algorithm runs in $\widetilde{O}(d\sqrt{W}/\varepsilon^3)$ time and returns a sketch from which one can derive estimates $(\widehat{\mathrm{cost}}_1,\ldots,\widehat{\mathrm{cost}}_n)$ satisfying $\sum_{k=1}^{n}\bigl|\widehat{\mathrm{cost}}_k-\mathrm{cost}_k\bigr| \le \varepsilon\,\mathrm{cost}(G)$. Thus, we obtain an $\ell_1$ approximation to the full profile whose error is at most an $\varepsilon$-fraction of the area under the true profile. In particular, this yields a $(1\pm\varepsilon)$-approximation to $\mathrm{cost}(G)$ within the same running time. We also prove a nearly matching lower bound of $Ω(d\sqrt{W}/\varepsilon^2)$ queries for estimating $\mathrm{cost}(G)$.

entry.title: Dissipative Dynamical Phase Transition as a Complex Ising Model
entry.summary: We investigate a quantum dynamical phase transition induced by the competition between local unitary evolution and dissipation in a qubit chain with a strong, on-site $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. While the steady-state of this evolution is always maximally-mixed, we show that the dynamical behavior of certain non-local observables on the approach to this steady-state is dictated by a quantum Ising model with a complex transverse-field (cTFIM). A crucial feature of our mapping to the cTFIM is an extensive number of local, weak, $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetries possessed by the dynamics, allowing us to investigate these observables analytically and uncover a dynamical phase transition as the relative rate of unitary evolution and dissipation is tuned. We show that the weak-dissipation limit corresponds to a cTFIM with a large magnitude of the imaginary transverse-field, for which the many-body "ground-state" (with smallest real eigenvalue) is gapless, exhibiting quasi-long-range correlations of the local magnetization with a continuously-varying exponent. Correspondingly, the dynamics of the non-local observables show oscillatory behavior with an amplitude decaying exponentially in time. The strong-dissipation limit corresponds to a gapped ferromagnetic phase of the cTFIM, and non-local observables show exponential decay on the approach to equilibrium. This transition in (1+1)-dimensions has a peculiar, "two-sided" nature appearing as either first- or second-order depending on the phase from which the transition is approached, an analytic result which is corroborated by numerical studies. In higher dimensions, we present a field-theoretic understanding of the first-order nature of this transition, when approaching from the ferromagnetic phase of the cTFIM, though the nature of the phase with large imaginary transverse-field remains to be understood.

entry.title: Superradiant scattering by rotating black-bounce black holes
entry.summary: We investigate superradiant scattering off a rotating regular black hole described by a black-bounce metric which generalizes the Kerr spacetime of mass $M$ and specific angular momentum $a$ through a regularization parameter $p$ and two deformation exponents $(k,n)$. Focusing on massless $(\ell,m)=(1,1)$ scalar modes, we explore the parameter space and compute amplification factors by numerically integrating the separated radial Klein-Gordon equation. We track the peak amplification and the corresponding frequency across the $(a/M,p/M)$ parameter space for several combinations of $k$ and $n$. We find that increasing $n$ systematically enhances superradiance, whereas increasing $k$ tends to suppress it. In particular, certain configurations can lead to amplification factors that significantly exceed the maximum amplification found for standard Kerr black holes.

entry.title: GKM Theory for Manifolds of Isospectral Matrices in Lie Type D
entry.summary: We study the manifold $Q_{Γ, λ}$ of isospectral real skew-symmetric matrices with a prescribed sparsity pattern determined by a graph $Γ$. The compact torus $T^n$ acts naturally on $Q_{Γ,λ}$ by conjugation, and this action can be studied using GKM theory. We prove two results about this manifold and its GKM graph. The first theorem describes how the GKM graph of $Q_{Γ, λ}$ is obtained from the GKM graph of the corresponding manifold $M_{Γ, λ}$ of isospectral Hermitian matrices. The second theorem shows that equivariant formality of $Q_{Γ,λ}$ implies equivariant formality of $M_{Γ,λ}$, whereas the converse fails.

entry.title: Hamming Ideals and Grobner Bases for ISD-like Syndrome Decoding
entry.summary: We investigate an algebraic approach to the Syndrome Decoding Problem, based on a reformulation of the Hamming weight constraint and its integration with the Information Set Decoding paradigm. We begin with a systematic analysis of the Hamming variety, deriving its defining equations in terms of elementary symmetric functions. Since these equations may have high degree, we exploit convolution identities for elementary symmetric functions, together with factorizations based on Lucas' identity, to derive an equivalent formulation with auxiliary variables and equations of bounded degree. Building on this modeling, we generalize the ISD paradigm through an ISD-like decoding strategy, implemented by the GBDecode algorithm, in which only a subset of an information set is fixed. This approach reduces the size of the combinatorial search space at the cost of solving the associated multivariate nonlinear systems. To handle this algebraic component, we employ the MultiSolve algorithm, which replaces a single Grobner basis computation with a collection of computations on simpler systems, obtained by exhaustively assigning a varying number of indeterminates over the finite field. This provides a tunable balance between combinatorial search and algebraic solving. We evaluate the resulting approach experimentally on instances of the Syndrome Decoding Problem for random binary linear codes, using parameters corresponding to the NIST Security Category 1 parameter set of the Classic McEliece cryptosystem. The experiments assess the feasibility of this combinatorial-algebraic approach and provide insights into the practical behavior of Grobner basis techniques within an ISD-like decoding framework.

entry.title: Partial Stabilizer Learning under Fixed Commuting Constraints and the Absence of a Copy-Rate Discount
entry.summary: We consider an unknown pure stabilizer state of \(n\) qudits with a fixed prime local dimension \(p\), together with prescribed commuting Pauli observables. Rather than learning the whole state, the learner must recover only complementary stabilizers that commute with the prescribed observables, together with their eigenvalues. Once the prescribed measurement is performed, this information and the observed outcome determine the corresponding conditional stabilizer state. We compare the number \(k\) of copies available to the learner with the number \(n\) of qudits and refer to their ratio \(k/n\) as the copy rate. Suppose that the dimension \(m\) of the requested complementary stabilizer subspace satisfies \(m=βn+o(n)\) for a fixed \(0<β\leq1\). If the copy rate converges to a value below one, the optimal exact recovery probabilities and verification scores converge to zero, both in the worst case and under the uniform prior. Conversely, if the number \(k\) of copies minus the number \(n\) of qudits tends to positive infinity, the entire stabilizer state can be identified with probability tending to one, and the requested complementary information can then be extracted. Thus, restricting the learning target to the stabilizer information needed after the prescribed measurement yields no copy-rate discount.

entry.title: Partitions in quantum theory
entry.summary: Decompositional theories describe the ways in which a global physical system can be split into subsystems, facilitating the study of how different possible partitions of the same system interplay, e.g. in terms of inclusions or signalling. In quantum theory, subsystems are usually framed as sub-C*-algebras of the algebra of operators on the global system. However, most decompositional approaches have so far restricted their scope to the case of systems corresponding to factor algebras. We argue that this is a mistake: one should cater for the possibility for non-factor subsystems, arising for instance from symmetry considerations. Building on simple examples, we motivate and present a definition of partitions into an arbitrary number of parts, each of which is a possibly non-factor sub-C*-algebra. We discuss its physical interpretation and study its properties, in particular with regard to the structure of algebras' centres. We prove that partitions, defined at the C*-algebraic level, can be represented in terms of a splitting of Hilbert spaces, using the framework of routed quantum circuits. For some partitions, however, such a representation necessarily retains a residual pseudo-nonlocality. We provide an example of this behaviour, given by the partition of a fermionic system into local modes.

entry.title: Criteria for Feasible Monte Carlo Stochastic Simulations of Bosonic Markovian Open Quantum Dynamics
entry.summary: The Monte Carlo sampling of the stochastic differential equations (SDEs) based on the quasiprobability distribution function, such as the Glauber--Sudarshan P, Wigner, and Husimi Q functions provides a powerful framework for investigating bosonic open quantum many-body dynamics described by the Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad (GKSL) equation, while considering the effects of quantum fluctuations beyond the mean-field approximation. However, the stochastic Monte Carlo simulation is possible only when the corresponding Fokker--Planck equation has a positive-semidefinite diffusion matrix, and the general conditions for the diffusion matrix to be positive semidefinite have remained unclear. In this work, starting from the path integral formulation, we first derive the sufficient conditions under which the diffusion matrix is positive semidefinite for an arbitrary Hamiltonian, jump operators, and choice of quasiprobability distribution functions. We also analytically derive the corresponding SDEs to be solved. We then investigate the dynamics of the GKSL equation in the thermodynamic limit and show that, depending on the form of the jump operators, the mean-field approximation may fail to describe the dynamics accurately, making stochastic Monte Carlo simulations indispensable. Furthermore, we derive the sufficient conditions under which the higher-order quantum fluctuation terms beyond the Fokker--Planck description vanish identically, even when the jump operators contain quadratic terms. Under these conditions, whenever the corresponding SDEs can be derived, the stochastic Monte Carlo simulation reproduces the exact dynamics. These results clarify the conditions under which the stochastic Monte Carlo simulations are both feasible and necessary for accurately describing the dynamics governed by the GKSL equation in phase space.

entry.title: Combining Adaptive Seamless Phase II/III Designs and Group Sequential Analysis for Time-to-Event Endpoints in Oncology Trials
entry.summary: Seamless Phase II/III designs are a natural vehicle for the randomized dose optimization called for by the US Food and Drug Administration's Project Optimus initiative. Their extension to group sequential repeated testing of a time-to-event endpoint after end-of-Phase-II dose selection, however, remains largely unestablished. Existing proposals index the boundaries for the post-selection looks by the overall information fraction of the primary endpoint---the correct index for the log-rank statistics of an unadapted trial, but not for the combination statistics these designs actually test---and support family-wise error rate (FWER) control by simulation. We instead work from the joint distribution of the combination statistics themselves, calibrating group sequential boundaries separately for each hypothesis in the closure and applying closed testing at every look; a general lemma establishes that this controls the FWER in the strong sense, for any number of hypotheses and analysis times. Specifically, under patient-wise separation and an inverse-normal combination test, the interim and final statistics for an individual hypothesis are bivariate normal, with a correlation determined by how the events at each look divide between the pre- and post-selection cohorts rather than by the overall information fraction, so that their boundaries follow from standard group sequential software; the corresponding statistics for the intersection hypothesis, formed from a Hochberg-adjusted Stage-1 $p$-value, are not multivariate normal, and we obtain their boundaries by a dedicated numerical integration. Head-to-head against a recently proposed incremental-Dunnett procedure, the two were near-identical when the design projections were correct, but ours was more robust when the combination weights were based on a misprojected division of the Stage~1 events either side of the interim.

entry.title: Negative Convexity in Pass-Through MBS: Mechanisms and Conditions
entry.summary: This paper investigates the mechanisms and conditions underlying negative convexity in pass-through mortgage-backed securities (MBSs) backed by fixed-rate mortgages. We first derive an exact decomposition of MBS prices into three components: the present value of interest-rate-independent cash flows, the present value of principal repaid early through interest-rate-dependent prepayments, and an interest rate option component capturing the reduction in future cash flows due to prepayments. Under a first-order approximation, the latter two components resemble portfolios of floorlets and Asian-style interest rate options, respectively. We then apply a cumulant expansion to derive closed-form valuation approximations under the one-factor Hull--White model. Numerical results show that including the second cumulant improves accuracy relative to a first-cumulant approximation. Building on the price decomposition, we decompose duration and convexity into component-level contributions and express the condition for negative convexity in terms of their second-order interest rate sensitivities. Finally, phase diagrams across interest rate levels and refinancing sensitivities identify the regions where negative convexity occurs and the corresponding sign boundaries. The negative-convexity region expands as the long-run mean of refinancing sensitivity increases. Negative convexity can arise even when no refinancing incentive exists initially, while its magnitude may vary nonmonotonically with the interest rate level. These findings explain negative MBS convexity through the sensitivities of its price components and quantitatively characterize the conditions governing its occurrence.

entry.title: Influence of Anthropisation on a Mosquito Community in a Tropical Forest-Village Interface
entry.summary: Tropical forests are undergoing deep changes caused by human activities, which have repercussions on the habitats of wild animal, particularly mammals. As mammals serve as a main source of blood meals for forest mosquitoes, their decline may affect the mosquitoes, as do changes in their habitats and abiotic conditions, such as rainfall, temperature, etc. Finally, along with humans come new species of mosquitoes-more generalist and more anthropophilic-that adapt to these new conditions and, moreover, serve as vectors for re-emerging diseases against which local populations have no more immunity. In this work, we derive a deterministic model which includes the effects of anthropisation, two species of mosquito that interact with one another (one is a generalist, whilst the other is sedentary and lives in the forest), and blood feeding preferences between multiple blood sources. We consider two socio-ecological areas, corresponding to a domestic area (for instance, a village), and a wild area (for instance, a tropical forest). A comprehensive analysis of the system is carried out using classical theory and monotone systems theory. We analyse the efficiency of individual protective measures, such as mosquito nets and repellents, against the domestic mosquito species. We investigate the risk of invasion of the wild area by a generalist mosquito species. We show that habitat anthropisation and high interspecific competition facilitate the invasion. When the mathematical system converges towards a periodic cycle, we provide numerical estimates for the periodic invasion threshold. Using a global sensitivity analysis, we show that the model is sensitive to the level of anthropisation, the adaptability of the invasive species to the forest area, and its fitness. The more efficient way to control the invasion is, therefore, to limit, as much as possible, the forest anthropisation.

entry.title: Geometry-controlled zeros of resonant Kelvin-wave conversion in four spatial dimensions
entry.summary: We show that geometry can suppress resonant four-wave conversion of Kelvin waves on a vortex surface in four spatial dimensions. Perpendicular incoming waves eliminate the entire local-area contribution, exposing a finite interaction mediated by the surrounding fluid. Reflection allows the incoming wave-number ratio to vary at exact resonance, revealing a sign-changing zero of this fluid coupling at \(λ_*\simeq1.469\). Uniform matching of the Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) four-wave coupling to the fluid result establishes microscopic zeros that approach this ratio at long wavelengths. Numerical calculations also show the corresponding sign change. Independent calculations in separate resonant geometries connect the coupling sign to the phase of coherently generated waves and the frequency ordering of reflection-even and reflection-odd modes. The surrounding flow thus determines whether an exactly resonant conversion channel is present at four-wave order.

entry.title: In-Context Learning for Multi-Fidelity Multiscale Model Closure and Cross-Operator Out-Of-Distribution Generalization
entry.summary: Multi-fidelity learning uses low-fidelity information (coarse-scale PDE models) together with limited high-fidelity data (fine-scale solutions) to obtain high-accuracy PDE solutions. It is a data-driven approach to downscale reduced-order models to solve PDEs efficiently and accurately. Standard multi-fidelity learning focuses on one operator or PDE; given a new PDE, retraining using additional coarse-fine solution pairs may be required, which is costly. In this work, we propose an in-context multi-fidelity learning framework for learning multiple multi-fidelity operators with one shared model. The model is trained using paired low- and high-fidelity examples as demonstrations from multiple operators, together with a new coarse-scale solution query, to predict the corresponding fine-scale solution. Once trained, given a new PDE operator, a few (fewer than five) coarse-fine demonstration pairs, and a low-cost coarse query, the model predicts the corresponding fine-scale solution without fine-tuning. When the target operator appears in the training dataset but has a different prediction goal, such as predicting beyond the training time interval, no additional demonstrations are needed. Instead, the model uses training coarse-fine pairs from that PDE and information from other training operators. Testing then only requires generating a low-cost coarse-scale solution query, without fine-tuning. Notably, our smallest model contains only 255,364 trainable parameters, corresponding to approximately 456 parameters per training operator for 560 operators.

entry.title: The extragalactic science of the KMOS VVVX-GalCen spectroscopic survey II: Discovery of a galaxy cluster at z = 0.089 behind the Galactic plane
entry.summary: The Zone of Avoidance (ZoA) continues to represent the most significant incompleteness in the extragalactic census of the Local Universe. It is evident that photometric surveys alone are insufficient to establish whether the galaxy overdensities detected therein are physical systems or projections along the line of sight. We present the first spectroscopic results of the extragalactic science area of the KMOS VVVX-GalCen Spectroscopic Survey, demonstrating how near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy can reveal and dynamically characterise galaxy clusters hidden by the Milky Way. A photometric overdensity of 19 galaxy candidates was identified in the VVV NIRGC III catalogue, centred at $(l,b)=(274.05^\circ,+2.85^\circ)$ with a mean interstellar extinction of $A_{K_s}=0.2$ mag; 16 of these candidates were observed with VLT/KMOS in the $HK$ grating and yielded spectra with reliable cross-correlation radial velocities. A total of 14 galaxies form a compact structure with a mean redshift of $\langle z \rangle = 0.089 \pm 0.001$, which corresponds to a mean radial velocity $\langle cz \rangle = 26660 \pm 170$ km/s, while two are foreground galaxies. The rest-frame line-of-sight velocity dispersion is $σ_v = 560^{+110}_{-120}$ km/s, implying an indicative dynamical mass of $M_{200} = 1.9^{+0.7}_{-1.1} \times 10^{14} M_\odot$ (based on members within the cluster core $\sim 0.4 r_{200}$) and placing the system in the poor-cluster regime. Of these 14 cluster members, 13 also lie within the $2σ$ scatter of the fitted near-IR red sequence. The other two galaxies are foreground objects that lie outside this range.
